title: A Refined Convergence Estimate for A Fourth Order Finite Difference Numerical Scheme to the Cahn-Hilliard Equation
abstractText: In this article we present a refined convergence analysis for a second order accurate in time, fourth order finite difference numerical scheme for the 3-D Cahn-Hilliard equation, with an improved convergence constant. A modified backward differentiation formula temporal discretization is applied, and a Douglas-Dupont artificial regularization is included to ensure the energy stability. In fact, a standard application of discrete Gronwall inequality leads to a convergence constant dependent on the interface width parameter in an exponential singular form. We aim to obtain an improved estimate, with such a singular dependence only in a polynomial order. A uniform in time functional bounds of the numerical solution, including the higher order Sobolev norms, as well as the associated bounds for the first and second order temporal difference stencil, have to be carefully established. Certain recursive analysis has to be applied in the analysis for the BDF-style temporal stencil. As a result, we are able to apply a spectrum estimate for the linearized Cahn-Hilliard operator, and this technique leads to the refined error estimate. A three-dimensional numerical example of accuracy check is presented as well.

title: Low-dimensional approximations of the conditional law of discrete-time Volterra processes: A non-positive curvature approach
abstractText: Predicting the conditional evolution of discrete-time Volterra processes with stochastic volatility is a crucial challenge in mathematical finance. While deep neural network models offer promise in approximating the conditional law of such processes, their effectiveness is hindered by the curse of dimensionality caused by the infinite dimensionality and non-smooth nature of these problems. To address this, we propose a two-step solution. First, we develop a stable dimension reduction technique, projecting the law of a reasonably broad class of discrete-time Volterra processes onto a low-dimensional statistical manifold of non-positive sectional curvature. Next, we introduce a sequentially deep-learning model tailored to the manifold’s geometry, which we show can approximate the projected conditional law of the considered Volterra process. Our model leverages an auxiliary hypernetwork to dynamically update its internal parameters, allowing it to encode non-stationary dynamics of the Volterra process, and it can be interpreted as a gating mechanism in a mixture of expert models where each expert is specialized at a specific point in time. Our hypernetwork further allows us to achieve approximation rates that would seemingly only be possible with very large networks.

title: Emerging and multidrug-resistant pathogens in retail leafy greens, Cape Winelands, South Africa
abstractText: Leafy greens are increasingly linked to outbreaks of foodborne diseases caused by opportunistic foodborne pathogens, such as Listeria monocytogenes and Salmonella species. Additionally, studies have reported antibiotic-resistant organisms, including foodborne pathogens, from fresh produce. Antibiotic resistance is a global health concern, as it may lead to treatment failure for subsequent infections. This study isolated antibiotic-resistant and multidrug-resistant L. monocytogenes, including those resistant to first-line antibiotics such as ampicillin, from ready-to-eat and whole leafy greens sold at major retailers in the Winelands region of the Western Cape, South Africa. Sixty leafy green samples from three commercial retailers were phenotypically screened for Listeria and Salmonella species and confirmed with the VITEK®2 compact automated system. Antibiotic susceptibility testing was done using the Kirby–Bauer disc diffusion method. Three isolates (5%) were confirmed as L. monocytogenes, along with one isolate each of L. seeligeri and L. rocourtiae. Additional species confirmed included emerging opportunistic pathogens such as Kocuria kristinae. No Salmonella spp. were confirmed. Instead, phenotypically presumptive colonies were identified as Enterobacter cloacae complex, Raoultella planticola, Citrobacter species and Klebsiella oxytoca. These isolates presented phenotypic resistance to clinical and veterinary antibiotics.

title: AI governance through the eyes of users: a large-scale study of online reviews
abstractText: Purpose With the growing importance of artificial intelligence (AI) governance, numerous high-level frameworks have been articulated by policymakers and expert communities to guide the development and application of AI. While such frameworks offer valuable normative orientation, they may not fully capture the practical concerns of those who interact with AI systems in organizational and operational contexts. This study aims to address that gap by exploring bottom-up, user-centered perspectives on AI governance. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a bottom-up approach to explore how governance-relevant themes are expressed in user discourse. Drawing on over 100,000 user reviews of AI products from G2.com, we apply Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers for Topic Modeling (BERTopic) to extract latent themes and identify those most semantically related to AI governance. Findings The analysis reveals a wide range of governance-relevant topics spanning technical and non-technical domains. These include concerns across organizational processes, such as planning, coordination, and communication, as well as stages of the AI value chain, including deployment infrastructure, data handling, and analytics. The findings show overlap with institutional AI governance frameworks on issues like privacy and transparency, while surfacing overlooked areas such as project management, strategy development, and customer interaction. Originality/value This paper advances AI governance research by introducing a scalable method for identifying governance-relevant topics using semantic similarity and unsupervised topic modeling. It offers a novel, bottom-up mapping of governance concerns as expressed in user discourse, highlights both alignments and blind spots in existing frameworks, and demonstrates how bottom-up user perspectives complement existing AI governance frameworks by revealing governance dimensions that are salient in practice.

title: THOR: A GPU-accelerated and MPI-parallel radiative transfer code
abstractText: Emission and absorption line features are important diagnostics for the physics underlying extragalactic astronomy. The interpretation of observed signatures involves making comparisons against forward-modeled spectra from galaxy formation simulations as well as more simplified geometries, while including the complex scattering radiative transfer (RT) of resonant emission lines. Here, we present þor, a modern C++ RT code focused initially on resonant emission lines. þor is a high-performance, distributed-memory, multi-target code that uses the message passing interface (MPI) for parallel execution. It runs on CPUs, GPUs, and other accelerators, yielding large ∼ 10-50 speed-ups compared to previous CPU-only codes. Our code supports multiple grid-based and grid-less data structures, enabling comparisons across different hydrodynamical codes as well as toy model geometries. We demonstrate its science capabilities with a number of example use cases across scales: (i) Lyman-alpha RT on simple shell-like gas distributions; (ii) Lyman-alpha RT applied to a high-resolution, high-redshift (z ∼ 6) cosmological hydrodynamical galaxy formation simulation; (iii) magnesium-II halos, namely, scattering and emission from the circumgalactic medium (CGM) of a z ≃ 1 galaxy drawn from a cosmological magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) simulation; (iv) the large-scale cosmic web in gas emission, a 6144^3 volume element RT scaling calculation; and (v) synthetic absorption spectra of the Lyman-alpha forest. We employed extensive verification and benchmarking to validate our approach and its computational efficiency. x

title: A study on creative activities for enhancing manual dexterity and visual-motor integration in older adults: focus on bamboo weaving
abstractText: Objective In the face of a rapidly aging society and the consequent rise in healthcare costs, maintaining the health of older adults and delaying functional decline to preserve their independence in daily living has become a critical issue in long-term care and healthcare development. This study examines the effects of creative activities on enhancing manual dexterity and visual-motor integration (VMI) in elderly individuals, with bamboo weaving selected as the intervention. Methods A total of 87 participants aged 60 to 75 were assigned to three groups (A, B, and C) based on varying levels of course difficulty. Pre- and post-intervention assessments were conducted using the Purdue Pegboard Test (PPT), VMI test, Visual Perception (VP), and Motor Coordination (MC) tests to evaluate the intervention outcomes. Findings indicated that participants across all levels demonstrated significant improvements post-intervention. Further analysis revealed that participants in the lower-difficulty courses showed better performance in the PPT assembly task as well as in the VMI and MC assessments. title: Loop quantum gravity black holes surrounded by quintessence
abstractText: Quantum gravity corrections act on the near-horizon geometry of a black hole (BH), while dark energy acts on its asymptotic region, and how the two imprints combine is still poorly understood. We study a static, spherically symmetric BH of Loop Quantum Gravity (LQG) surrounded by a quintessence field. The metric function carries the LQG parameters [Formula: see text] and the quintessence parameters [Formula: see text], and for suitable values it has three horizons, a structure found neither in pure LQG BHs nor in classical quintessence BHs. We analyze null and timelike geodesics, photon spheres and the shadow seen by a static observer placed between the event and the cosmological horizons. Sixth-order WKB quasinormal modes (QNMs) of scalar and electromagnetic fields confirm stability over the ranges examined. The quantum term behaves as a short-range repulsive correction: it shrinks the photon sphere and the shadow, raises the QNM oscillation frequency and lowers the light deflection. Quintessence works the other way on the photon sphere, the ringing frequency and the bending. With the Gauss–Bonnet method, we obtain a weak deflection angle valid for [Formula: see text], which we check against direct numerical integration, and in which quintessence dominates at large impact parameters and the LQG terms at small ones.

title: Photometric classification of supernovae detected by the Zwicky Transient Facility using noise augmentation
abstractText: Modern time-domain surveys, such as the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF), detect far more extragalactic transients than can be spectroscopically classified. Photometric classification offers a scalable alternative, enabling the identification of larger, fainter, and higher-redshift supernova (SN) samples suitable for applications such as Type Ia SN (SN Ia) cosmology. We present a feature-based photometric classifier for SNe detected by ZTF, with the primary goal of constructing a photometric SN Ia sample for cosmological analyses. Our approach utilises the autoencoder architecture from the model to capture the intrinsic diversity of SN light curves. We trained the model on a spectroscopically classified ZTF SN sample, incorporating a realistic redshift and augmentation procedure that simulates the flux uncertainties of fainter sources. This enables the model to generalise to noisier, higher-redshift populations. Light curve features were used to train a gradient-boosted decision tree classifier, implemented in both binary (SN Ia vs non-Ia) and multi-class configurations. We validated our classifier on independent, fainter ZTF data with and without augmentation. To evaluate real-time performance, we also applied our classifier to live ZTF alerts and conducted a spectroscopic classification survey within the ePESSTO+ collaboration. ParSNIP We found that redshift and noise augmentation significantly improves classification performance, particularly for fainter sources. Our binary classifier achieves an SN Ia recall of $(98.1 ± 0.4)%$, averaged across five train–test splits. SN Ia recall exceeds 98% for events with more than 10 detections and a peak apparent magnitude of up to 20, remaining above 96% up to a magnitude of 20.5. Overall, 95% of the sources were correctly classified in both binary and multi-class modes. In our live classification survey, we correctly identified the class for 78% of the targets, including rare events such as superluminous SNe, despite a median of only nine detections per object. Our classifier performs efficiently on real ZTF data, including faint and noisy light curves. Applied to the full ZTF transient sample, it will enable the construction of a large photometric SN Ia dataset for cosmology. It also provides a practical tool for real-time spectroscopic target prioritisation, which will be essential for large-scale surveys such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s Legacy Survey of Space and Time.

title: Development of a multicomponent mindfulness and movement program for lumbosacral radicular pain: protocol for a mixed methods feasibility study
abstractText: Background Lumbosacral radicular pain (LRP) is a highly disabling condition frequently accompanied by pain-related fear, reduced physical activity, and difficulty engaging in daily activities. Although mindfulness-based and movement-based interventions are recommended for chronic low back pain, few programs have been specifically designed for individuals with LRP or developed using patient-centered, theory-informed methods. Before large-scale evaluation, early-phase work is needed to establish the feasibility and acceptability of such interventions and their associated study procedures. This protocol describes the development and pilot testing of Move-MORE, a multicomponent, digitally delivered mindfulness and movement intervention for adults with LRP and elevated kinesiophobia. Methods This study uses an iterative convergent mixed methods design comprising two sub-studies. Study 1 is a qualitative-dominant intervention development study involving patient focus groups (n = 10) and clinician interviews (n = 10) conducted using the Person-Based Approach to refine intervention content and delivery. Study 2 is a single-arm feasibility trial (n = 32) enrolling adults aged 18–75 with LRP and elevated kinesiophobia. Move-MORE will be delivered virtually in a group format with primary outcomes of feasibility and acceptability, including recruitment, retention, adherence, engagement, safety, and data completeness. Acceptability will be assessed using validated satisfaction and expectancy measures and qualitative exit interviews. A comprehensive set of patient-reported outcomes, ecological momentary assessment, actigraphy, quantitative sensory testing, and biomechanical assessments will be collected to characterize participants, evaluate data collection procedures, and inform outcome selection and design considerations for a future randomized controlled trial. Quantitative analyses of patient-reported outcomes and objective assessments will be descriptive. Finally, patient partners were involved throughout the study using a patient-engaged research approach, including participation in focus groups to inform intervention development, review of participant-facing materials, and input on interpretation and dissemination of study findings. Discussion This protocol outlines a systematic, patient-engaged approach to developing and testing the feasibility of a novel multicomponent intervention tailored to individuals with LRP. Findings will inform refinement of the Move-MORE intervention and methodological decisions needed to support subsequent efficacy testing in a randomized trial. Trial registration Clinicaltrials.gov #: NCT07125027; Registration Date: August 9th, 2025.

title: The Geography of Nobel Prize Nomination, 1901–1975
abstractText: Nobel laureates are concentrated in a few countries, yet where geographic sorting enters the prize’s selection pipeline remains unknown. From archival, parliamentary, and web sources we construct a five-layer network built around the nomination records of five prizes, 1901–1975, with 512,793 edges and 8,133 identified participants. Although Swedish and Norwegian bodies administer the prizes, the nominators who actually took part were geographically diverse. Within that pool, however, nominators chose same-country nominees 4.85 times as often as random matching would predict. This homophily ratio ranges by discipline from 8.58 in Literature to 3.01 in Physics. With matching restricted to the same prize and year, the ratio is still 3.3. The continent-level ratio rose through the 1940s and stayed elevated as the nominee pool kept diversifying. A model that adjusts for how many nominations each country sent and received yields a roughly fifteenfold same-country premium, still sevenfold after adjusting for shared language. Nominations that crossed geographic regions flowed asymmetrically, with Northern America the dominant net importer. A nominee’s same-country nomination share was negatively associated with eventually winning the prize. In sum, across the stages we can observe, geographic sorting concentrates at the discretionary nomination decision, beyond what the nominator pool’s composition predicts.

title: Scale for autism in females (SAF): a diagnostic interview for the female phenotype
abstractText: Purpose This study aimed to develop preliminary validity evidence for the Scale for Autism in Females (SAF), a semi-structured diagnostic interview designed to capture the often-overlooked presentation of autism in girls. For decades, autism assessment has been shaped primarily by male-centered diagnostic frameworks, contributing to the under-recognition of many females. Using a Delphi-style expert review process, experienced clinicians evaluated the SAF across three rounds of review. Findings provided initial evidence of face and content validity and informed revisions to strengthen the scale. As an early-stage instrument, the SAF represents a first step toward more inclusive, gender informed assessment practices. Design/methodology/approach This study used a qualitative Delphi-style design to support the initial development and preliminary validation of the SAF, a clinician-guided semi-structured diagnostic interview designed to assess the female autism phenotype. Twenty-eight experienced clinicians with expertise in autism diagnosis participated in 3 rounds of structured expert review. Using the Content Analysis and Evaluation Protocol rubric, participants evaluated each item’s clarity, representativeness, importance and utility while also providing feedback. Quantitative ratings were analyzed and thematic analysis of written responses guided iterative revisions to strengthen the SAF’s face and content validity and clinical applicability. Findings Findings provided strong preliminary evidence of the SAF’s face and content validity. Across three rounds of expert review, clinicians consistently rated SAF items highly in clarity, representativeness, importance and clinical utility, with all items ultimately exceeding the established consensus threshold. Qualitative thematic analysis identified five major themes that informed iterative revisions to the measure, including differentiation from neurotypicality, level of insight, gender and sexuality considerations, clinician training gaps and formatting improvements. Feedback led to revisions that strengthened the scale’s accessibility, organization and clinical relevance. Overall, results supported the SAF as a promising early-stage tool for identifying the female autism phenotype. Research limitations/implications These findings highlight the growing need for assessments that recognize the experiences of autistic women rather than relying primarily on male-centered diagnostic frameworks. The SAF offers clinicians a structured way to explore camouflaging, internalized social difficulties and relational patterns that contribute to delayed or missed diagnosis. The study also underscores ongoing gaps in clinician training surrounding the female autism phenotype. However, the SAF remains an early-stage instrument. Limitations include a relatively small and demographically homogeneous expert sample and the absence of direct validation from autistic females. Future research should include psychometric validation, normative data, factor analysis and clinical comparison studies. Practical implications The SAF represents an early but important step toward more inclusive and gender informed autism assessment practices and, to our knowledge, is the first diagnostic interview developed with the female autism phenotype at the core of its conceptualization. By exploring experiences such as masking, social exhaustion and compensatory coping strategies, the SAF expands beyond the externally observable behaviors emphasized in traditional assessments. Although further psychometric validation is needed, the SAF may support earlier identification and more affirming diagnostic experiences in clinical, school, outpatient and multidisciplinary assessment settings while increasing clinician awareness of subtle female autism presentations. Social implications The SAF has important social implications for autistic women who have historically been overlooked, misunderstood or diagnosed later in life due to male-centered diagnostic frameworks. More accurate recognition of autism improves access to educational supports, mental health services and community resources while reducing experiences of isolation and chronic masking. Diagnoses also affect not only the individual, but their families, educators, peers and support systems by increasing understanding and helping others respond with greater empathy. Although still in the early stages of development, the SAF represents a step toward more inclusive diagnostic practices that better reflect the diversity of autistic experiences. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, the SAF is the first clinician-guided diagnostic interview developed with women at the center of its conceptualization rather than treating female presentations as secondary to male-centered diagnostic frameworks. This study contributes an early but meaningful step toward addressing the long-standing underrecognition of autistic women in research and clinical practice. By centering experiences of compensatory coping strategies, the SAF seeks to amplify presentations that have historically been overlooked or misunderstood. Beyond assessment, the SAF may also serve as a clinician training framework that encourages more inclusive, affirming and equitable approaches to autism identification across settings.

title: On the number of missing integers in partitions
abstractText: In the preceding decade, Andrews and Newman resurrected the concept of a “minimal excludant” of a partition ([Formula: see text], for short), namely, the least positive missing integer in a partition. Subsequently, several authors have not only studied its generalizations, analogs and the like but also connected the mex to several important partition statistics. In this paper, we study the set of missing positive integers as a whole, in two different classes of partitions, namely, unrestricted partitions and overpartitions. To be precise, a [Formula: see text] is a positive integer that is less than the largest part of a partition and which does not occur as a part. In particular, we examine the number of partitions with a given number of missing integers, determine congruences for two pairs of functions associated to them, and propose three bias type inequality conjectures for these functions.

title: Preprints Without Curation Are Increasingly Cited by Journals
abstractText: The recent strain on peer review systems necessitates publicizing knowledge before formal review. Citing a preprint was traditionally permitted only if marked as provisional and under review; now, preprints remaining only on servers (non-curated preprints) are cited without such indication. Linking six major preprint servers to the world’s largest bibliographic reference database and restricting to top-journal citations, we compare citation rates with a null model of authors indifferent between preprints and vetted articles. Preprints are cited 5-10 times less often than their share of the literature predicts, yet journal articles are increasingly likely to cite preprints, a rise robust since 2013 and exceeding what exponential submission growth alone would produce. Confounding factors (faster publishing cycles, a few highly cited preprints) cannot explain this shift. Unexpectedly, the COVID-19 pandemic did not amplify this growth but coincided with a deceleration in citation rates. These findings indicate a structural shift in citing behavior: preprints are increasingly perceived as credible regardless of later publication status, motivating attention to how citation conventions and journal policies should accommodate their expanding role. Our evidence comes from biology, where preprint adoption has expanded rapidly beyond arXiv’s strongholds of physics and mathematics; generalizability to other disciplines remains open.

title: Persistent right ventricular dysfunction and hemodynamic evolution predict in-hospital deterioration in intermediate-high- and high-risk pulmonary embolism
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Risk stratification in acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is based primarily on findings obtained at hospital admission. However, whether serial assessment of right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and hemodynamic changes provides incremental prognostic value beyond the initial risk stratification remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate longitudinal clinical and imaging variables associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes in patients with intermediate-high- and high-risk acute PE. METHODS: This prospective registry included patients with intermediate-high- and high-risk acute PE. The primary composite endpoint comprised in-hospital mortality, invasive mechanical ventilation, persistent shock or hypotension, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Longitudinal variables were assessed 24-72 hours after admission. All statistical tests were two-tailed, and a p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed, and discriminative performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC). A prespecified missing-data analysis was performed to assess the availability of follow-up computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA). RESULTS: The primary composite endpoint occurred in 21.2% of the 151 patients, with an in-hospital mortality rate of 9.3%. Persistent RV dysfunction on follow-up CTPA (χ2 = 15.48; p < 0.001) and follow-up systolic blood pressure (SBP; p < 0.001) were the strongest individual predictors of adverse outcomes. In the longitudinal multivariable model (n = 60), persistent RV dysfunction on follow-up CTPA (OR 9.70; 95%CI, 1.96-47.89; p = 0.005) and follow-up SBP (OR 0.90; 95%CI, 0.83-0.96; p = 0.003) remained independent predictors. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination (AUC-ROC = 0.874) and adequate calibration. The missing-data analysis showed that patients without follow-up CTPA were more severely ill at baseline, consistent with a missing not at random mechanism. CONCLUSIONS: Reassessment of established risk markers during hospitalization may improve identification of patients who remain at high risk despite initial risk classification and treatment. Persistent RV dysfunction and lower follow-up SBP were independently associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes, which supports the use of dynamic risk stratification in acute PE.

title: Effects of acupuncture on arterial hypertension and endothelial dysfunction: the AHEaD trial
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Sympathetic overactivity, oxidative stress, and impaired nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation are key mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of hypertension. Acupuncture may decrease blood pressure by modulating autonomic nervous system activity, increasing NO bioavailability, attenuating sympathoexcitatory responses, and promoting vasodilation. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether acupuncture decreases peripheral systolic blood pressure (pSBP), peripheral diastolic blood pressure (pDBP), central systolic blood pressure (cSBP), central diastolic blood pressure (cDBP), and pulse wave velocity (PWV), and improves flow-mediated dilation (FMD). METHODS: This prospective, single-blind, placebo-controlled, single-center randomized clinical trial included adults with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension who were at low cardiovascular risk and were not receiving antihypertensive therapy. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group receiving manual acupuncture (n = 14) or a control group receiving nonpenetrating sham acupuncture (n = 16). Both groups underwent two 30-minute sessions per week for 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in pSBP measured at baseline (V1), after 12 weeks of treatment (V2), and at the 30-day end-study visit (V3). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups. At V2, acupuncture decreased pSBP by 13.2 mmHg (p = 0.003) and increased FMD by 2.7% (p = 0.016). In the control group, pSBP decreased by 4.1 mmHg (p = 0.035), whereas FMD increased by 1.6% (p = 0.029). Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in pSBP (-9.1 mmHg, p = 0.006) and FMD (+3.0%, p = 0.037) at V2. These between-group differences remained significant at V3 (pSBP: -8.4 mmHg, p = 0.038; FMD: +2.9%, p = 0.028). CONCLUSION: Acupuncture significantly improved endothelial function and decreased pSBP in adults with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension who were not receiving antihypertensive therapy after 12 weeks of treatment.

title: An evaluation of and tutorial for an open-source, web-based application for many-facet Rasch measurement
abstractText: This methods tutorial introduces a freely available, web-based tool that allows researchers to perform many-facet Rasch measurement (MFRM) without requiring extensive programming skills. The paper first reviews the use of Rasch measurement models in applied linguistics and highlights the limited availability of free and accessible tools specifically designed for MFRM. To address this gap, we introduce langtest (https://langtest.jp/), a web-based platform that hosts a wide range of statistical analyses commonly used in applied linguistics, including a newly developed MFRM module. The module provides functions for model estimation, model diagnostics, visualization, bias analysis, and reporting within a single analytical environment. We then provide a step-by-step tutorial using an openly available dataset to demonstrate the implementation and interpretation of MFRM in langtest. To evaluate the usefulness of the module, we compare key parameter estimates and diagnostic statistics produced by langtest with those obtained from Facets, a widely used standalone program for MFRM. The results show a high degree of convergence between the two programs across key MFRM outputs. These findings support the use of langtest as a freely available and accessible option for MFRM. We hope that langtest will facilitate wider adoption of MFRM and more transparent and reproducible measurement practices in applied linguistics research.

title: Effect of metal sleeve integration on implant placement accuracy using additively manufactured tooth-supported surgical guides: an in vitro study
abstractText: Background This in vitro study evaluated whether metal sleeve integration influences crestal horizontal, crestal vertical, and angular implant-placement deviations when additively manufactured tooth-supported surgical guides are used. Methods Thirty-two partially edentulous maxillary resin models were allocated to two groups: tooth-supported surgical guides with metal sleeves and sleeveless guides (n = 16 per group). Both guide designs were generated from the same virtual implant plan and manufactured using LCD-based vat photopolymerization. A VEGA implant measuring 4.0 × 10 mm was placed at the maxillary right first molar (FDI 16) in each model under standardized laboratory conditions. After implant placement, scan abutments were connected and the models were digitized using a laboratory scanner. The postoperative STL files were aligned with a master reference STL generated from a physical reference model intended to reproduce the planned implant position. Crestal horizontal, crestal vertical, and angular deviations relative to this master reference were measured. Between-group differences were assessed using the Mann–Whitney U test, with the significance level set at α = 0.05. Results No statistically significant differences were identified between the sleeveless and metal-sleeved groups for crestal horizontal deviation (median: 0.36 vs. 0.28 mm; p = 0.287), crestal vertical deviation (median: 0.53 vs. 0.63 mm; p = 0.402), or angular deviation (median: 8.00° vs. 10.00°; p = 0.171). Conclusions Under the conditions of this in vitro study, no statistically significant differences were detected between the metal-sleeved and sleeveless groups in crestal horizontal, crestal vertical, or angular deviation. Because the study was designed to test between-group differences rather than equivalence, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that the two guide designs are equivalent. Further studies using prespecified equivalence margins and clinical settings are required.

title: Cross-simulator transfer with foundation-model summaries: Toward robust SKA-era reionization inference
abstractText: Simulation-based inference (SBI) for parameter estimation is vulnerable to model misspecification: neural summaries and density estimators trained on a specific forward model typically fail when applied to data drawn from another model or from real observations, and no training simulator can capture the full observational pipeline of a real measurement exactly. We show that a self-supervised vision transformer (ViT), pretrained label-free on a fast approximate simulator, produces transferable data summaries that generalize across simulators. Without retraining, it can be reused as a frozen encoder to infer astrophysical parameters from a completely different simulator that explicitly resolves radiative transfer and on which it was never trained. As a concrete use case in 21cm cosmology, SKATR, a ViT pretrained with a self-supervised Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), serves as a foundation model for reionization inference from upcoming Square Kilometre Array (SKA) measurements: SKATR was pretrained once on 67k low-cost, noiseless semi-numerical 21cmFAST light cones, frozen, and applied to hydrodynamical Loreli II light cones, where a lightweight conditional flow matching (CFM) head infers five astrophysical parameters. The encoder is never shown Loreli data, its parameters, or any noise. In our comparison, SKATR yields the most precise and best-calibrated posteriors across all five parameters, matching the accuracy of the fully supervised in-domain baseline while requiring 2.6 fewer radiative-transfer simulations. Under realistic SKA AA* noise, only SKATR remains simultaneously accurate, informative, and calibrated, outperforming even a supervised baseline retrained from scratch on noisy data. Self-supervised pretraining on computationally efficient semi-numerical simulations is therefore a viable route to calibrated, simulator-, and noise-agnostic reionization inference for the SKA-era.

title: CARD: A Configurable Approximate Restoring Divider for Image Processing Applications
abstractText: This paper proposes a new Configurable Approximate Restoring Divider (CARD) to alleviate the tradeoff between accuracy and efficiency in unsigned array dividers. Configurable restoring subtractor cells (CRSCs), which can operate in both exact and approximate modes, are utilized as the fundamental building blocks in the design of CARD. These cells replace exact subtractor cells within the array structure, causing minimal effects on the output quotient bits when operating in approximate mode under the triangular replacement scheme. Various accuracy metrics and hardware characteristics have been evaluated for a 16-bit/8-bit unsigned configurable restoring divider. Synthesis results show that the proposed CARD uses 50% fewer resources, requires only 95 LUTs, achieves twice the speed, and consumes 40% less power compared to a conventional exact divider. The proposed CARD is coded in Verilog-HDL, implemented on the Artix-7 FPGA (XC7A35T-ICPG236C) board, and synthesized with Xilinx Vivado simulator. It demonstrates substantially higher accuracy while maintaining hardware characteristics similar to those of other reconfigurable designs. An image processing application is also presented to evaluate the functionality of the proposed CARD.

title: Repensar la eficiencia. Relevancia epistémica y evaluación del diseño de artefactos
abstractText: Este artículo propone una reconceptualización de la relevancia epistémica en el campo del diseño y la evaluación de artefactos. A partir de una crítica a los enfoques centrados exclusivamente en la eficiencia funcional, se argumenta que el valor de un artefacto no se agota en su rendimiento técnico, sino que incluye dimensiones afectivas, simbólicas y situadas. El artículo desarrolla una tipología ampliada de eficiencias, vinculada con los niveles de experiencia del usuario, y examina cómo los artefactos median formas de atención, conocimiento y modos de habitar. A través del ejemplo de distintas cafeteras, se sostiene que los artefactos no son objetos neutrales, sino agentes que incorporan puntos de vista y configuran relaciones epistémicas. Se concluye que un diseño relevante no es solo eficiente, sino capaz de transformar nuestros modos de existencia.

title: La Agencia argentina de promoción CTI. Evolución institucional, ejecución presupuestaria e instrumentos de promoción orientada (1996-2023)
abstractText: En este artículo se observa la evolución institucional de la Agencia I+D+i de Argentina, la ejecución de su presupuesto y los instrumentos de promoción orientada que gestionó. Estos tres elementos permiten sopesar cuidadosamente la relación entre los desafíos de política pública asumidos como propios y la acción estatal efectivamente implementada. Primero se reconstruye el marco histórico en el cual se creó la Agencia y las principales transformaciones institucionales que atravesó, para llegar a establecer etapas e hitos institucionales a lo largo de las últimas tres décadas. Luego se analiza la ejecución presupuestaria en relación con la matriz de gastos de la Función Ciencia y Técnica del presupuesto nacional para rastrear algunos rasgos distintivos de la Agencia, como su especial relevancia en las transferencias a otros organismos y la gestión del financiamiento externo. Finalmente, se analiza la evolución de los instrumentos de promoción desplegados entre 2008 y 2023, con especial atención a los instrumentos orientados gestionados al interior del FONARSEC.

title: Water boosts the formation of refractory sulfur in interstellar ices
abstractText: Sulfur is the tenth most abundant element in space, yet it is strongly depleted in the gas phase of dense interstellar regions, suggesting sequestration in dust grain components that are difficult to detect. We study whether UV irradiation and thermal processing of H_2S-containing interstellar-ice analogues can produce refractory sulfur species, and whether water-dominated ice enhances their formation. We performed UV irradiation and warm-up experiments on H_2S-containing ice analogues with and without water, and the resulting refractory residues were analysed ex situ. Refractory sulfur species, including the sulfur allotropes S_6--S_8, are formed during UV irradiation and thermal processing of H_2S-containing interstellar-ice analogues. Water enhances the formation of these sulfur allotropes by two orders of magnitude. A formation mechanism is proposed in which the ionic intermediates, identified in the reported experiments, stabilised by the water-ice matrix, promote chain growth and cyclisation, yielding predominantly S_8. The combined detection in our residues of S_ and polythionic species (H_2S_ also reported in meteorites and samples returned from asteroids, supports the idea that they formed in pre-cometary ice mantles covering dust grains. Because these species can incorporate multiple sulfur atoms per molecule, they constitute an efficient solid-phase reservoir for the `missing sulfur' in the dust of dense cloud environments where young stars are born. Refractory sulfur can therefore serve as a tracer of water-ice environments in space. We provide substantial evidence of the reaction pathway yielding sulfur deposits proposed in this work.

A mountain of nomenclatural mess: Revisiting Sennen’s “endemic taxa” from Tibidabo (Barcelona, Spain) through typifications and taxonomic notes with a focus on Asteraceae
abstractText: Frère Sennen, a prominent botanist in the early 20th century, made significant contributions to the field through his extensive collection and distribution of plant specimens to institutions worldwide. However, his nomenclatural proposals have been criticised for their redundancy and interpretational challenges. This study focuses on reevaluating the plant taxa mentioned by himself as endemic to Tibidabo mountain in Barcelona, updating their names according to modern floras and typifying them when possible. Of the 75 nomenclatural proposals investigated, 59 are considered validly described and 42 have been lectotypified in the present study. Only Hieracium barcinonense (Cichorieae, Asteraceae) is typified here as an accepted species.

The role of artificial intelligence in change management: ethical and organizational culture implications
abstractText: Purpose This paper examines the accelerating integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into organizational change management (OCM). It explores AI's dual role as both a powerful facilitator of change and a continuous disruptor itself, focusing specifically on the ethical and cultural challenges it introduces to traditional operational and decision-making frameworks. Design/methodology/approach Employing a narrative literature review approach, this study synthesizes 47 peer-reviewed journal articles, conference proceedings, relevant practitioner papers and book chapters published since 2010. The review systematically analyzes the literature on the integration, impact and long-term consequences of applying AI in OCM contexts. Findings The review underscores AI's transformative capacity to reshape OCM from a traditional, linear process into a dynamic, continuous “meta-change” formalized here as an integrative process linking AI's technological properties to three generative mechanisms, two governing elements and OCM outcomes expressed as four theoretical propositions. While AI enhances change efficiency, it also introduces significant cultural and ethical hurdles, including algorithmic bias, identity threat among management and the unintended reshaping of workplace culture and norms. The findings indicate that successfully navigating this change landscape requires a strategic shift toward staged implementation, organizational agility, cultural alignment, effective ethical policies and, most importantly, human-AI symbiosis, underpinned by Explainable AI (XAI) to foster workforce trust. Research limitations/implications The research advances the conversation around AI in managing the change process and emphasizes the need for dynamic and human-oriented interventions to work in parallel with AI. Future research should explore long-term implications of AI adoption in OCM, focusing on the interplay between technological advancements and organizational culture. Investigating sector-specific nuances and developing strategies to address workforce adaptation, resistance and continuous learning are critical areas for further study. Practical implications Organizations can utilize AI to personalize change strategies, foster agility and support data-driven decisions. Leaders should emphasize ethical AI implementation and workforce upskilling to ensure successful integration and maintain trust. Collaborative frameworks that combine human intuition with AI insights are essential for achieving sustainable outcomes. Social implications Social implications including understanding the workforce displacement, upskilling and changes in organizational culture aligned to any integration of AI in the management of organizational change. While AI enhances efficiency, it may fuel inequalities, automate routine tasks and challenge human–AI collaboration dynamics. Ethical concerns like algorithmic bias and accountability impact trust and fairness, while rapid transitions can cause employee stress and resistance. A broader societal effect could be economic polarization and ethical use of AI. Originality/value This paper bridges the critical gap between theoretical discourse on AI-driven OCM and practical, ethical implications and implementation. While AI's potential to optimize change is widely recognized, existing research remains fragmented regarding the ethical governance and cultural frictions associated with its adoption. By identifying emergent themes from the narrative literature review, this study offers a theoretically grounded agenda for “meta-change,” reconciling technological agility with human-centric governance in AI-enabled organizational change.

title: Ce-doped CuO/Mg(OH) 2 nanocomposites: Structural, optical, thermal and multifunctional properties
abstractText: Multifunctional nanocomposites with tuneable properties have attracted attention for environmental and biomedical applications. Ce incorporation can modify their structural, optical, thermal and functional properties. In this work, PVP (polyvinylpyrrolidone) capped Ce-doped CuO/Mg(OH) 2 nanocomposites were successfully synthesized using the co-precipitation method. Three synthesized samples are identified in this paper by the sample codes NC1, NC2 and NC3: undoped CuO/Mg(OH) 2, 2[Formula: see text]mol% Ce-doped CuO/Mg(OH) 2 and 4 mol% Ce-doped CuO/Mg(OH) 2, respectively. All samples were explored with various analytical characterization techniques to study the influence of Ce incorporation on multifunctional properties of the nanocomposites. XRD confirmed the polycrystalline nature of nanocomposites, consisting of monoclinic CuO and hexagonal Mg(OH) 2 phases, with a slight decrease in crystallite size upon Ce incorporation. TEM and FESEM analyses revealed the nearly spherical and sheet-like morphologies, while EDS spectra and elemental mapping confirmed the presence and distribution of Cu, Mg, O and Ce. FT-IR analysis identified various functional groups present in nanocomposites, whereas XPS confirmed the oxidation states of Cu[Formula: see text], Mg[Formula: see text] and Ce[Formula: see text]/Ce[Formula: see text]. TGA-DSC analysis revealed weight loss and thermal decomposition behavior of the nanocomposites. UV–visible DRS analysis exhibited low reflectance below 700 nm and a reduction in optical bandgap energy with increasing Ce concentration. The 4[Formula: see text]mol% Ce-doped CuO/Mg(OH) 2 nanocomposite exhibited 95.67% degradation of methyl orange and 98.11% of methylene blue within 120 and 60[Formula: see text]min, respectively, under UV–visible irradiation. The same sample achieved 90.43% DPPH free radical scavenging activity. The antibacterial assays of 4[Formula: see text]mol% Ce-doped CuO/Mg(OH) 2 nanocomposites exhibited zones of inhibition (ZOI) of [Formula: see text][Formula: see text]mm and [Formula: see text][Formula: see text]mm, against bacteria strain Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis), respectively. Thus, the synthesized Ce-doped CuO/Mg(OH) 2 nanocomposites represent a new class of multifunctional materials with potential applications in photocatalysis, antioxidant and antibacterial activity.

title: Dual-layer ultra-thin polarization-insensitive metamaterial for ultra-wideband microwave absorption
abstractText: This work proposes a dual-layer ultra-thin polarization-insensitive metamaterial for ultra-wideband microwave absorption. The proposed metamaterial absorber (MMA) consists of two resistive frequency selective surfaces (RFSS) constructed in a grounded dielectric substrate. The two RFSSs, although with the same unit cell periodicity, have different geometric patterns and significantly different surface impedances, resulting in distinct reflection, transmission and absorption properties. The independent electromagnetic simulations of the two RFSSs provide their reflection and transmission coefficients. Leveraging these simulation results, a detailed theoretical analysis based on interference theory predicts that the MMA can achieve ultra-wideband absorption. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the MMA achieves over 90% absorption from 4.3[Formula: see text]GHz to 31.3[Formula: see text]GHz under normal incidence of arbitrarily polarized waves. Its total thickness is merely 5.3[Formula: see text]mm, thus yielding a high bandwidth-to-thickness ratio (BTR) of 11.35. Moreover, the MMA exhibits good angular stability, for incident angles up to 60 ∘, its absorptivity under transverse-magnetic (TM) wave incidence remains above 97% across the frequency band of 8.7–33.7[Formula: see text]GHz. Finally, experimental measurements on a fabricated sample further validate the absorption performance of the MMA. Overall, the proposed MMA can achieve ultra-wideband absorption and has a higher BTR compared to numerous previous designs, making it highly attractive in practical applications.

title: Three-body corrections to the Brownian viscosity of hard spheres without hydrodynamic interactions
abstractText: For Brownian hard spheres without hydrodynamic interactions, we study the part of the contact stress produced by three-body correlations: the third-order coefficient of the zero-shear Brownian viscosity. Kirkwood superposition gives zero for this coefficient: three nonzero pair contributions cancel exactly. An elementary radial identity exposes the cancellation, and evaluating closures with the same contact stress makes their coefficients directly comparable. Although superposition solves the bulk equation, it leaves a flux error on each shared contact. This error defines a unique finite-energy weak correction whose positive diffusive dissipation, suitably normalized, is a weak-energy coefficient. Explicit symmetric trials yield a variational lower bound and a residual upper bound, and exact integration with outward rational arithmetic proves that the weak-energy coefficient lies between 1.8266948 and 1.8267157. For the physical viscosity coefficient this is a conditional interval: the two coefficients coincide when the physical three-body correction equals the weak correction and the remote remainder of the pair adjoint identity, a surface term at large pair separation, vanishes. The interval excludes every closure coefficient compared here, including the zero of superposition. Hydrodynamic interactions contribute at the same orders in real suspensions, where rheometry measures total viscosities, so the coefficient is a quantitative benchmark for theories and simulations of dilute three-body Brownian stress in this model.

title: Group 3 malignant proliferating trichilemmal tumor of the scalp: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Malignant proliferating trichilemmal tumor (MPTT) is a rare cutaneous adnexal neoplasm with heterogeneous biological behavior, and initial clinical or histopathological misdiagnosis as a benign cyst is common. We report a case of Group 3 (high-grade) MPTT according to the three-tier histological classification of Ye et al, which groups these tumors by stromal invasion and cytologic atypia, to describe the histological features that support this classification and the consequences of fragmented excision of a presumed benign cyst. CASE SUMMARY A 58-year-old woman presented with a left temporal scalp mass, stable at about 1 cm for at least 5 years, that enlarged rapidly over the preceding two months, clinically resembling a trichilemmal cyst. Physical examination revealed a well-demarcated, soft lesion measuring 22 mm, with no cervical lymphadenopathy. Contrast-enhanced cervical and thoracic computed tomography showed no evidence of regional or distant lymphadenopathy. The lesion was completely excised; histopathology demonstrated proliferative trichilemmal epithelium with severe cytological atypia, mitotic activity, early stromal infiltration, and desmoplastic stroma, without lymphovascular invasion, classified as Group 3 (malignant) according to the Ye et al criteria. Because the specimen was fragmented, margins could not be assessed. Wide re-excision with 1-cm margins down to the periosteum achieved tumor-free margins. The patient received adjuvant radiotherapy (50 Gy in 12 fractions) and remains free of recurrence or metastasis at 6 months after the end of radiotherapy. CONCLUSION A scalp cyst that is stable for years and then enlarges rapidly should be excised intact and examined histologically. This case shows that a Group 3 tumor can be diagnosed even when invasion is limited and the specimen is fragmented; the short follow-up requires caution.

title: Clinical, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic features of childhood cardiomyopathy in the United Arab Emirates
abstractText: BACKGROUND Cardiomyopathy (CMP) is one of the main causes of heart failure in children. Genetic and metabolic etiology are common in regions with high consanguinity. AIM To describe the clinical, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic features of childhood CMP in the United Arab Emirates. METHODS This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in the United Arab Emirates, covering a period from 2020 to 2025. Historical data back to January 2013 were retrieved for survival analysis. All children with CMP were included. Demographic, clinical, electrocardiography, and echocardiography (echo) data were collected. Metabolic and genetic studies were included. RESULTS The study included 200 cases of CMP (60% were female). The cohort comprised 25 ethnic groups, with consanguinity status known for 70 families and positive in 31%. The most common age of presentation was 0-6 months. Syndromic features and neurodevelopmental delays were found in 28% and 33% of the cases, respectively. Long QT syndrome was diagnosed in 9% of the patients. Metabolic screening was positive in 15% of the cohort. The most common abnormalities were conditions associated with high lactate levels (31%), followed by conditions associated with high ammonia levels (15%). Genetic testing was positive in 21.5% of the cohort. The most common genetic abnormality was Noonan’s syndrome, followed by Alström and CHARGE syndromes; the latter, to our knowledge, has not been previously reported. Hypertrophic CMP (HCM) was the most common type (47%), followed by dilated CMP (36.5%), noncompaction CMP (14%), and restrictive CMP (2.5%). Patients with HCM presented significantly earlier and had more associated syndromic features (P < 0.041). There was statistically higher mortality in patients with noncompaction CMP associated with low EF or with HCM (combined) and a higher recovery rate in those with DCM (P < 0.05). The whole cohort mortality rate was 12%, and it was 25% for those with positive genetic testing. The mean (95%CI) of overall survival was 73.8 months. There were significantly lower survival rates in patients with edema. CONCLUSION In this highly consanguineous population, CMP is more prevalent in females and presents mostly in early infancy. The most common type is HCM. Genetic and metabolic disorders are common and are associated with higher mortality rates.

title: Electric Vehicle Charge Scheduling and Power Trading Using Shuffle Attention Network Enhanced by Star Bison Optimization
abstractText: The growth of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has increased the demand for smart charging systems that optimize energy usage and reduce strain on the power grid. The current EV charging strategies are often uncoordinated, resulting in peak load issues and increased energy costs. An efficient scheduling scheme is required to align charging with grid conditions. Hence, a new Shuffle Attention Network with Star Bison Optimization Algorithm (SA-Net_StarBOA) is established for EV Charge Scheduling and Power Trading. Primarily, an EV system with multiple Charge Stations (CS) and EVs is simulated. Then, charging scheduling is performed using the devised StarBOA, which is a combination of Star Fish Optimization (SFOA) and African Bison Optimization (ABO). Here, power prediction is done by the Shuffle Attention-Network (SA-Net) for predicting the availability of charging power. Besides, if the power is not available for charging the vehicle, then optimal electricity trading is done by SA-Net. Here, SA-Net is trained with the developed StarBOA model. Furthermore, SA-Net_StarBOA acquired a low average waiting time of 5.100 seconds (s), distance of 39.464 meters (m), the number of charged EVs of 145 and power of 96.580 Watts (W) at iteration 1,000.

title: Role of novel inflammatory indices in predicting major adverse cardiovascular events following revascularization in chronic limb-threatening ischemia
abstractText: BACKGROUND Peripheral artery disease is a prevalent atherosclerotic condition leading to chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), which significantly increases the risks of limb loss and cardiovascular events. Despite advancements in revascularization techniques, long-term outcomes remain poor. AIM To evaluate the association of pre-procedural inflammatory indices with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) following lower-limb revascularization in patients with CLTI, and to assess the predictive performance of clinical models incorporating Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII), Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI), and Systemic Immune-Inflammation Response Index (SIIRI). METHODS A multicenter prospective observational study was conducted at two tertiary hospitals in Jordan, including 303 adults (≥ 18 years) with CLTI undergoing lower-limb revascularization between June and September 2024. Participants were followed for six months. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics and pre-procedural inflammatory indices were obtained, and MACE was identified through follow-up and confirmed using medical records. Three multivariable logistic regression models were developed using the same clinical and laboratory covariates, with SII, SIRI, and SIIRI entered separately. The predictive performance of the SIRI-based model was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis and 1000 bootstrap resamples for internal validation. RESULTS The mean age of participants was 63.6 ± 9.8 years, and 84.5% were male. Overall, MACE occurred in 22.4% of patients. The incidence of MACE increased across Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection clinical stages, from 12.5% in the low-risk group to 17.7% in the moderate-risk group and 29.0% in the high-risk group (P = 0.038). Surgical revascularization was also more frequent among patients who developed MACE (30.5% vs 18.8%, P = 0.023). In multivariable analysis, SIRI was independently associated with MACE (odds ratio = 1.62, 95%CI: 1.156-2.279; P = 0.005). The SIRI-based model demonstrated strong discrimination, with an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.937 (95%CI: 0.907-0.967), which remained robust after bootstrap internal validation, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.920. CONCLUSION SIRI was independently associated with MACE in patients with CLTI undergoing lower-limb revascularization and demonstrated strong discriminatory performance when incorporated into a multivariable clinical model. These findings suggest that SIRI may provide additional prognostic information beyond established clinical and laboratory characteristics and may have potential utility for cardiovascular risk stratification in this high-risk population. Further external validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Structural and Electrochemical Characterization of Na2CO3/ γ- Al2O3 Electrodes for Supercapacitor
abstractText: The development of electrode materials with suitable structural and surface properties is crucial for improving electrochemical energy storage systems. Gamma alumina (𝛾-Al2O3) has attracted considerable interest in electrochemical research due to its unique structural and surface properties. However, its charge-storage capacity is still limited, highlighting the need for structural and compositional modifications to improve its electrochemical performance. In this study, Na2CO3 was introduced into 𝛾-Al2O3 as a sodium precursor to induce phase modification and enhance the electrochemical activity. The systematic incorporation of Na2CO3 also provides an opportunity to elucidate the relationship between compositional changes, structural evolution, and electrochemical response. 𝛾-Al2O3 was modified with different Na2CO3 contents (0, 10, 20, and 30%) through a solution-based mixing method. XRD results indicate that Na2CO3 addition affects the γ-Al2O3 structure and promotes the formation of a secondary NaAlO2 phase. SEM analysis reveals an increase in particle size and porosity with increasing Na2CO3 concentration, with porosity increasing from 42.37% to 48.38%. The CV profiles exhibit quasi-rectangular characteristics, indicating a pseudocapacitive contribution arising from redox reactions occurring at the electrode surface. Increasing Na2CO3 concentration also reduces the Rs and Rct, reaching 13.37 Ω and 49.67 Ω, respectively, at 30% Na2CO3. GCD measurements show that the specific capacitance increases from 2.737 to 7.844 F g-1, while the energy density and power density reach 1.151 Wh kg-1 and 27.045 W kg-1, respectively. Among the compositions studied, the electrode with 30% Na2CO3/ -Al2O3 showed the improvement in electrochemical properties.

title: Effect of preheating palm oil biodiesel fuel on the performance and emissions of diesel engine common rail direct injection
abstractText: Fossil fuel consumption continues to increase while its reserves continue to decrease and produce high emissions that trigger global warming. Therefore, more environmentally friendly alternative energy is needed. Biodiesel is a sustainable choice because it is biodegradable, low in sulphur, and can replace fossil fuels. This study investigates the influence of biodiesel fuel preheating temperature on engine performance, fuel consumption, and emissions in a Common Rail Direct Injection (CRDI) diesel engine. The experimental method was carried out by heating B40 and B50 fuels at temperatures of 40°C to 60°C at intervals of 10 °C. Engine performance was evaluated using a chassis dynamometer at engine speeds of 1500 to 3000 rpm at intervals of 500 rpm, fuel consumption was measured with a digital scale, and exhaust emissions testing was carried out using an opacity smoke meter. Fuel preheating at 60°C in B40 and B50 blends improved engine performance, where power output increased by up to 1.03% (78.3 vs 77.5 HP), torque rose by up to 2.64% (178.6 vs 174 Nm), BSFC reduced by up to 7.30%, and opacity emissions decreased by up to 40% compared to fossil diesel. Fuel preheating improves atomization and promotes cleaner combustion in a diesel engine.

title: Coenzyme Q10 for heart failure and symptomatic cardiovascular diseases
abstractText: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10, ubiquinone), embedded within the inner mitochondrial membrane, fulfills a dual physiological mandate as an essential electron shuttle in the oxidative phosphorylation cascade and an endogenous antioxidant. Heart failure (HF) and ischemic heart disease (IHD) are characterized by profound tissue CoQ10 depletion. Pivotal randomized controlled trials, including the landmark Q-SYMBIO study, in which 93% of participants had heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), have demonstrated that exogenous CoQ10 supplementation ameliorates functional capacity and significantly mitigates the risks of cardiovascular mortality and HF rehospitalization. Furthermore, CoQ10 confers robust anti-anginal and anti-ischemic cytoprotection in patients with coronary artery disease by preserving endothelial nitric oxide synthase coupling, suppressing lipid peroxidation, and augmenting ischemic preconditioning. 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase inhibition suppresses mevalonate pathway downstream synthesis of CoQ10, occasionally precipitating statin-associated muscle symptoms or statin-induced cardiomyopathy-a rare yet severe metabolic complication readily reversible upon prompt CoQ10 repletion. Despite these benefits, substantial clinical knowledge gaps persist regarding the therapeutic efficacy of CoQ10 in microvascular angina and HF with preserved ejection fraction. This narrative review critically evaluates the biomechanical mechanisms of CoQ10 in cardiomyocyte contractility, synthesizes rigorous clinical trial evidence across HFrEF and IHD, examines statin-induced mitochondrial depletion, and delineates future translational directions for addressing unmet needs in cardiovascular medicine.

title: A Risk-Aware Stratified Undersampling Method for Imbalanced Software Defect Prediction
abstractText: Software defect prediction (SDP) suffers from severe class imbalance, as defective samples typically account for less than 20% of the data, which often leads to biased model training and degraded prediction performance. Undersampling has been widely used to address class imbalance and improve prediction performance. However, existing undersampling methods may alter the original data distribution by removing majority-class samples, potentially displacing the learned decision boundary in real-world SDP scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposes a risk-aware undersampling method for software defect prediction, which aims to alleviate class imbalance while reducing discrepancies between the retained and original majority-class distributions. The proposed method quantifies feature importance using SHAP values, incorporates defect distribution patterns to calculate a risk score for each majority-class sample, and performs proportional random sampling within decile-based risk strata. Experiments on 19 public datasets evaluate the proposed method. The results show that RASU achieves the highest average F1-score, MCC, and AUC under the decision-tree classifier and remains competitive under SVM and Random Forest. Ablation and controlled synthetic experiments indicate that the stratification mechanism can mitigate decision-boundary displacement under the evaluated settings.

title: Qixiong Zuogui-preconditioned mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes protect the neurovascular unit in aged rats subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion
abstractText: BACKGROUND Neurovascular unit (NVU) dysfunction is a key pathological mechanism underlying neurological impairment in elderly patients with ischemic stroke (IS). Mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-Exos) have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality for IS. Qixiong Zuogui Compound (QXZG), a traditional Chinese herbal formula with kidney-tonifying and blood-activating properties, may potentiate the protective effects of MSC-Exos in IS; however, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unexplored. AIM To investigate whether QXZG-preconditioned MSC-Exos (QXZG-Exos) promote neurological recovery by modulating the NVU in rats with D-galactose-induced aging subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). METHODS High-throughput sequencing was used to compare the microRNA (miRNA) expression profiles of MSC-Exos treated with blank serum or QXZG-containing serum. Differentially expressed miRNAs were screened and subjected to bioinformatic analysis to identify key biological processes and major signaling pathways. Candidate miRNAs were further validated by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. In addition, rats with D-galactose-induced aging subjected to MCAO/R were used to evaluate the protective effects of QXZG-Exos on NVU integrity. Molecular biology techniques were used to comprehensively analyze the effects of QXZG-Exos on various NVU components and to assess whether they inhibit inflammatory responses and restore NVU homeostasis, potentially through modulation of the sirtuin 1 (SIRT1)/nuclear factor kappa B p65 (NF-κB p65) pathway. RESULTS High-throughput sequencing identified 56 differentially expressed miRNAs. Gene Ontology enrichment analysis revealed significant involvement in biological processes, including the inflammatory response, whereas Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway analysis identified the NF-κB signaling pathway and cellular senescence as key target mechanisms. Animal experiments confirmed that QXZG-Exos improved NVU ultrastructure, enhanced neuronal nuclei expression, downregulated glial fibrillary acidic protein, and upregulated cluster of differentiation 31 and vascular endothelial growth factor A, thereby reducing neuronal damage and blood-brain barrier permeability and ultimately protecting the NVU. In addition, QXZG-Exos ameliorated neurological deficits and pathological injury and improved learning and memory after MCAO/R. Mechanistically, QXZG-Exos upregulated SIRT1 expression and suppressed NF-κB p65 and its downstream inflammatory factors by modulating the SIRT1/NF-κB pathway. CONCLUSION QXZG may modulate miRNA expression profiles in MSC-Exos, thereby improving NVU structural integrity and attenuating inflammatory injury. These effects may be associated with regulation of the SIRT1/NF-κB pathway.

title: Dynamics of a modified Leslie–Gower eco-epidemiological model with fear effect, carry-over effect, and time-varying delay
abstractText: In this study, a modified Leslie–Gower time-varying delay eco-epidemiological model with fear effect, fear carry-over effect, and cooperative hunting is investigated. First, the positivity and boundedness of solutions for the delay-free system, as well as the stability of equilibria are discussed, and sufficient conditions for the global asymptotic stability of the positive equilibrium are obtained. Then, taking the fear effect parameter and the fear carry-over effect parameter as bifurcation parameters, the Hopf bifurcation near the positive equilibrium is studied. Furthermore, the effects of time delay on system stability are analyzed, and the conditions for the occurrence of delay-induced Hopf bifurcation are derived. Next, to suppress the periodic oscillations caused by time delay, a time-varying delay perturbation is introduced as a control strategy, and the critical condition for oscillation suppression is obtained using the method of multiple scales. Finally, the parameter sensitivity analysis is conducted. The numerical results show that changes in the fear effect and fear carry-over effect can drive the system from a stable coexistence state to a periodic oscillatory state. Once the time delay exceeds a critical threshold, the system loses stability and exhibits sustained oscillations, however a suitable time-varying delay perturbation can effectively suppress these oscillations and restore the system to a stable state.

title: Trial architecture in contemporary cardio-oncology: Why parallel-group randomized controlled trials may not fit every cardiotoxicity phenotype
abstractText: Cardio-oncology has evolved rapidly with immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted kinase inhibitors, yet cardiovascular prevention strategies remain largely informed by evidence generated during the anthracycline era. This critical narrative review examines why cardioprotection trials have failed to keep pace with these evolving toxicity mechanisms, analyzing trial populations, endpoint selection, biomarker strategies, imaging approaches, and overall trial design across traditional and newer cancer therapies, rather than summarizing therapeutic efficacy. The evidence shows a persistent mismatch between contemporary toxicity phenotypes and existing trial design: Most studies continue to focus on anthracycline-associated left ventricular dysfunction and surrogate imaging endpoints, while immune-mediated myocarditis, cytokine release syndrome-related cardiomyopathy, vascular toxicities, arrhythmias, and other emerging phenotypes remain inadequately represented, compounded by limited biological stratification, one-size-fits-all prevention strategies, heterogeneous outcome definitions, and insufficient mechanism-specific monitoring. Progress in cardio-oncology prevention is constrained not only by the availability of candidate cardioprotective interventions but by the near-uniform persistence of a single trial architecture across mechanistically distinct toxicities. Future studies should adopt phenotype-driven, mechanism-informed, adaptive trial designs using clinically meaningful outcomes that reflect the diversity of contemporary cardiovascular toxicities.

title: Creative Design Transformations: From Plain to Stylized Cloth Patterns Using Sam and Stable Diffusion Generative Model
abstractText: Advances in image processing and artificial intelligence have brought about a substantial revolution in the design industry, particularly in image inpainting techniques, which have improved accuracy, originality, and creative patterns. Image inpainting restores blurred or corrupted areas of an image while enabling the creation of diverse visual patterns. This research focuses on transforming plain fabric designs into stylized cloth patterns using text-based prompts. It leverages a Vision Transformer (ViT)-based pretrained segment anything model (SAM) and the stable diffusion (SD) inpainting model to achieve precise, high-quality pattern generation. SAM ensures accurate object segmentation by precisely defining regions for modification, where SD concentrates on high-fidelity, photorealistic images with context-aware improvements and seamless transformations. By integrating these models (ViT-SAM-SD), visually appealing fabric patterns can be generated from text, offering greater control and innovation in design. The performance of the ViT-SAM-SD model is compared with MaskGiT, StyleGAN2, PSGAN and VQGAN-based prompt-driven models with textile prompts. title: Putative role of helminths in mucosal regeneration for tissue engineering of gastrointestinal tract: A hypothesis
abstractText: Helminths are increasingly recognized as important modifiers of gastrointestinal (GI) homeostasis, while anthelmintic resistance is a growing challenge in veterinary and human medicine. GI tissue engineering has advanced rapidly through organoid-based constructs, cell sheets, and biomaterial scaffolds designed to restore damaged intestinal tissue. Clinical translation, however, occurs in a lumen densely populated by microbiota and, in some hosts, helminths, creating a complex biotic environment that may influence graft integration, infection risk, mucosal healing, and stem cell behavior. While bacterial and viral effects on GI regeneration are well studied, the role of helminths remains largely overlooked. This review focuses on two central themes: How GI helminths may shape regenerative responses, and how anthelmintic resistance affects the safety and feasibility of tissue-engineering strategies. We discuss how helminths may alter immune tone, epithelial renewal, and microbial composition; how resistant helminths may complicate pre-operative infection control; and how these factors intersect with antimicrobial resistance and microbiota-dependent regulation of intestinal stem cells. We also consider whether helminth-derived molecules could serve as controlled pro-regenerative tools, while noting that most translational applications remain preliminary. Rather than presenting the helminth-microbiota-tissue regeneration triad as an established model, we frame it as a conceptual hypothesis for organizing current evidence and identifying key research gaps.

title: Computing charged anisotropic compact stars in f(Q,T) gravity: Probing the lower mass gap through matter–non-metricity coupling
abstractText: The viability of stable compact stellar configurations within the lower mass-gap regime poses a significant challenge to conventional descriptions of neutron stars based on general relativity and standard equations of state. In this work, we investigate whether the interaction between non-metricity and matter can provide an additional mechanism to sustain supermassive compact configurations. To this end, we study charged anisotropic stellar models based on the [Formula: see text] gravitational formulation, considering the linear form [Formula: see text]. By implementing the extended gravitational decoupling approach and a charged Krori–Barua seed solution, we obtain an exact interior configuration smoothly matched to an exterior Reissner–Nordström spacetime. The resulting solutions satisfy all standard requirements of physical acceptability, including regularity, positivity of the thermodynamic variables, causality, energy conditions, hydrostatic equilibrium, and dynamical stability. We show that the matter–non-metricity coupling substantially increases the maximum supported mass, allowing stable stellar configurations to extend into the observational lower mass-gap region while remaining consistent with current pulsar and gravitational-wave measurements. The outcomes of our analysis indicate that [Formula: see text] gravity offers a viable geometric mechanism to alleviate the tension between observed massive compact objects and the limits predicted within general relativity.
