title: A FINITE PATTERN METHOD FOR EDGE-BASED DISTANCE INVARIANTS ON SELF-SIMILAR FRACTAL NETWORKS
abstractText: The exact analytical computation of edge-based distance invariants on self-similar fractal networks presents a fundamental challenge in fractal network theory: while vertex-based invariants have been extensively studied, their edge counterparts require handling boundary contributions and distance interactions across self-similar copies, for which no systematic method has been established. This paper proposes the finite pattern method, a general technique that leverages strict self-similarity to reduce the infinite global sum over edge pairs to a finite system of recursive equations. The method consists of three steps: classification of all relative position patterns between pairs of basic self-similar copies, derivation of edge-distance formulas for each pattern, and construction of linear recurrences governing the pattern counts. We demonstrate the method on the Sierpinski hexagon skeleton network, a canonical self-similar fractal, and obtain the exact closed-form expression for its edge-Wiener index — the core edge-based distance invariant. The 12 fundamental patterns arising from the six-fold rotational symmetry are fully enumerated, and the resulting recurrence system is solved explicitly. The finite pattern method is independent of the specific geometry of the Sierpinski hexagon and applies to a broad class of deterministic fractal networks generated by iterated function systems, providing a unified framework for the exact solution of edge-based distance invariants on self-similar structures.

title: Exosomal miR-148a-3p from adipose-derived stem cells promotes microglial M2 polarization and alleviates traumatic brain injury via the TMEM9B/NF-κB axis
abstractText: BACKGROUND Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, with no effective pharmacological therapy currently available. Adipose-derived stem cell exosomes (ADSC-Exos) have emerged as a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy, but the underlying molecular mechanisms, particularly the role of exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs) in regulating microglial polarization, are not fully understood. AIM To investigate whether ADSC-Exos alleviate TBI-induced neuroinflammation by delivering miR-148a-3p to microglia and promoting M2 polarization through the transmembrane protein 9B (TMEM9B)/nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) pathway. METHODS ADSC-Exos were characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and Western blot. A rat TBI model was established by the weight-drop method, and neurological recovery was assessed by the modified neurological severity score and the Morris water maze test. BV2 and primary microglial cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide to induce M1 polarization and then treated with ADSC-Exos or engineered exosomes. Subsequently, miRNA sequencing, quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, Western blot, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and functional rescue experiments were performed. RESULTS ADSC-Exos significantly improved neurological function in TBI rats, reducing the day-28 modified neurological severity score from 7.8 ± 1.2 (TBI) to 4.3 ± 0.9 (P < 0.001). In vitro , ADSC-Exos were internalized by microglia and promoted a shift from M1 to M2 polarization, increasing the proportion of CD11b⁺CD206⁺ cells from 5.8% ± 0.6% to 32.5% ± 2.8% (P < 0.001). MiRNA profiling identified miR-148a-3p as highly enriched in ADSC-Exos (4.8-fold vs ADSCs, P < 0.001). miR-148a-3p-mimic-exosomes recapitulated the anti-inflammatory effects, and dual-luciferase reporter assay confirmed that miR-148a-3p directly targeted TMEM9B, reducing luciferase activity by 62% (P < 0.01). Overexpression of TMEM9B in the rescue experiment largely abrogated ADSC-Exo-induced M2 polarization. Mechanistically, ADSC-Exos suppressed the NF-κB pathway by reducing phosphorylated p65 and IκBα levels. CONCLUSION ADSC-Exo miR-148a-3p promotes microglial M2 polarization and attenuates TBI via specific inhibition of the TMEM9B/NF-κB signaling axis, highlighting this pathway as a novel therapeutic target for neuroinflammatory disorders.

title: EGR1-P21 axis promotes a stromal senescence-like phenotype and impairs enteric neural crest cell migration in Hirschsprung disease
abstractText: BACKGROUND Hirschsprung disease (HSCR) is the most common congenital cause of functional intestinal obstruction in neonates, resulting from incomplete colonization of the distal bowel by enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs), a migrating population of multipotent neural crest-derived progenitors. Mutations in cell-autonomous regulators account for fewer than half of cases. Incomplete penetrance suggests non-cell-autonomous contributors residing in the intestinal microenvironment, but their molecular identity has remained largely undefined. AIM To identify and mechanistically characterize a stromal fibroblast program that contributes to impaired ENCC migration in HSCR. METHODS In this multimodel mechanistic study with correlative patient-tissue validation, paired aganglionic, transitional and ganglionic colonic segments from three HSCR patients were profiled by bulk RNA sequencing under a paired design and tested by quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction and Western blotting. Early growth response 1 (EGR1) was overexpressed by adenovirus in primary mouse embryonic intestinal fibroblasts (EMFs) and by lentivirus in human HFL-1 cells. Proliferation, apoptosis, senescence and extracellular matrix (ECM) output were quantified by immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, Western blot, quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction and senescence associated-beta-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining. Transwell migration and wound-healing assays were used to assess ENCC and SH-SY5Y cell migration in coculture. CUT&RUN-qPCR on primary EMFs and a dual-luciferase reporter in HEK293FT were used to test promoter occupancy and transactivation. Small interfering RNA-mediated CDKN1A knockdown in HFL-1 cells was used to test P21 dependence of the fibroblast phenotype. RESULTS EGR1 was upregulated stepwise from ganglionic to transitional to aganglionic colonic segments (n = 16 paired patients), enriched in fetal-gut fibroblasts, and aligned with the ENCC colonization window. EGR1 overexpression in EMFs increased fibronectin 1, COL1A1 and COL3A1, suppressed proliferation, attenuated apoptosis and induced a senescence-like phenotype (SA-β-gal-positive cells 39.30% ± 2.39% vs 6.52% ± 1.71%; n = 3 biological replicates); these findings were reproduced in HFL-1 cells. EGR1-overexpressing fibroblasts impaired ENCC and SH-SY5Y migration (approximately 40% reduction; n = 3). CUT&RUN-qPCR and luciferase assays showed EGR1 enrichment at the CDKN1A promoter and approximately 5-fold transactivation that was abolished by mutation of the GC-rich element. CDKN1A knockdown partially reversed the ECM, proliferation, survival and senescence-like phenotypes in fibroblasts; its effect on migration was not tested. HSCR patient tissues showed concordant aganglionic > transitional > ganglionic increases in ECM components and SA-β-gal positivity. CONCLUSION EGR1 activates CDKN1A in EMFs inducing a senescence-like, ECM-remodeling state that impairs ENCC migration in vitro ; paired HSCR tissues show a concordant but correlative signature. The EGR1-P21 axis is a candidate stromal mechanism in HSCR awaiting validation in disease-relevant systems.

title: Factors associated with one-year mortality in patients with hyponatremia hospitalized in a cardiology department: An exploratory retrospective cohort study
abstractText: BACKGROUND Hyponatremia is a common electrolyte disorder in hospitalized cardiac patients and is associated with increased mortality. However, data on factors associated with one-year mortality in patients with hyponatremia in real-world clinical practice are limited, and the temporal relationship between in-hospital predictors and long-term outcomes remains uncertain. AIM To explore factors associated with one-year mortality in cardiac inpatients with hyponatremia and assess the robustness of these associations in sensitivity analyses. METHODS This retrospective single-center cohort study included 119 patients (mean age 71.2 ± 12.7 years, 48.7% female) hospitalized in a cardiology department with hypotonic hyponatremia. Patients with acute coronary syndrome and/or myocardial infarction were excluded. The primary endpoint was all-cause death within 1 year, ascertained through the regional electronic death registry. Cox regression was used. Sensitivity analyses excluding in-hospital deaths and Firth’s penalized Cox regression were performed. RESULTS The one-year mortality rate was 44.5% (53/119). In the primary multivariable Cox model, stage II chronic heart failure (CHF) [hazard ratio (HR) 8.86; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.81-43.39; P = 0.007], minimum sodium (HR 0.94; 95%CI: 0.89-1.00; P = 0.040), and peak creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) (HR 1.02; 95%CI: 1.00-1.04; P = 0.002) were associated with one-year mortality. However, in a sensitivity analysis excluding in-hospital deaths, these associations were no longer statistically significant. In Firth’s penalized model, CK-MB (HR 1.02; 95%CI: 1.01-1.04; P = 0.007) and stage II CHF (HR 6.60; 95%CI: 1.67-33.37; P = 0.007) remained significant, whereas minimum sodium did not (P = 0.117). Non-linearity was not detected for sodium (P = 0.459) or CK-MB (P = 0.182). CONCLUSION In this exploratory analysis, CK-MB and stage II CHF were more robustly associated with one-year mortality than hyponatremia. The sodium association was not confirmed in sensitivity analyses. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

title: Vessel-level patterns and predictors of discordance between computed tomography coronary angiography and invasive coronary angiography
abstractText: BACKGROUND Coronary calcification is a recognized source of computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA) stenosis overestimation. We evaluated whether discordance between CTCA and invasive coronary angiography (ICA) also shows clinically relevant vessel-territory patterns in a selected real-world paired-imaging cohort. AIM To evaluate patient- and vessel-level CTCA diagnostic performance, quantify territory-specific discordance, assess three-category stenosis agreement, and identify predictors of discordance in a selected paired-imaging cohort. METHODS We systematically screened the hospital CTCA database for October 2019-December 2024 and included consecutive adults with paired CTCA and ICA within 120 days, subject to the study exclusions. After reviewing interval revascularisation, we excluded one patient in whom percutaneous coronary intervention occurred after diagnostic ICA but before the subsequent CTCA, leaving 403 patients and 1612 major epicardial vessel observations. Severe/occlusive disease was the positive binary endpoint, with a left main coronary artery (LMCA)-specific severe threshold of ≥ 50% in both modalities. Patient-level predictors were assessed with logistic regression and vessel-level predictors with mixed-effects logistic regression using a patient random intercept. RESULTS ICA demonstrated severe/occlusive disease in 204/403 patients (50.6%). Patient-level sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were 91.7% (95%CI: 87.0%-95.1%), 35.2% (95%CI: 28.6%-42.2%), 59.2% (95%CI: 53.5%-64.6%), and 80.5% (95%CI: 70.6%-88.2%), respectively. Across 1612 vessels, sensitivity was 80.8% (cluster-bootstrap 95%CI: 76.3%-85.1%), specificity 81.7% (95%CI: 79.5%-83.7%), PPV 50.4% (95%CI: 45.4%-55.2%), NPV 94.9% (95%CI: 93.5%-96.1%), and discordance 18.5% (95%CI: 16.6%-20.3%). At least one discordant vessel was present in 229 patients (56.8%). Discordance was highest in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) (31.8%) and lowest in the LMCA (2.5%). Three-category agreement was moderate (weighted kappa 0.500, 95%CI: 0.459-0.539). Calcium burden remained independently associated with discordance at the patient level [odds ratio (OR) = 1.66 per category, 95%CI: 1.03-2.73; P = 0.042] and vessel level (OR = 1.40, 95%CI: 1.04-1.87; P = 0.025). The LAD had higher adjusted odds of discordance than the right coronary artery (OR = 1.82, 95%CI: 1.32-2.53; Holm-adjusted P = 0.0003) and left circumflex artery (OR = 2.01, 95%CI: 1.44-2.80; Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). CONCLUSION In this selected cohort of patients who underwent both CTCA and ICA, greater visual coronary calcium burden was associated with anatomical discordance, and discordance varied by epicardial territory, being highest in the LAD. Because referral for ICA was selective, study readings were not independently blinded, and ICA stenosis was visually graded, the observed diagnostic metrics may not generalise to unselected CTCA populations. No downstream testing pathway, invasive-referral decision, or patient outcome was evaluated; the findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

title: Reply: Thymoquinone targets endoplasmic reticulum stress to rescue tendon stem cell identity - a new era for tendinopathy therapy
abstractText: Zhang provided a thoughtful and comprehensive appraisal of our study “Thymoquinone inhibited the chondrogenic differentiation of tendon-derived stem cells caused by tendon injury”, and placed our findings within the broader context of tendon biology and endoplasmic reticulum stress research. We greatly appreciate his constructive insights and have addressed each of the points raised in his commentary “Thymoquinone targets endoplasmic reticulum stress to rescue tendon stem cell identity - a new era for tendinopathy therapy”, including the limitations of our methodology and the complex relationship among unfolded protein response activation, oxidative stress, and cytokine signaling. Zhang’ s comments provide valuable guidance for our future investigations. We will employ an improved in vitro model using uniaxial cyclic mechanical stretching and co-culture techniques. Additionally, animal studies will incorporate histopathological grading and biomechanical assessment. The interactions among unfolded protein response activation, oxidative stress, and cytokine signaling will also be systematically investigated.

title: Xin-II shows cardioprotective effects in a rat model of chronic heart failure: An integrated network pharmacology and transcriptomic
abstractText: BACKGROUND Chronic heart failure (CHF) is a major global public health burden. Mongolian Medicine Xin-II has shown promising clinical efficacy in the management of cardiovascular diseases, including coronary heart disease and arrhythmias. However, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. AIM To evaluate the therapeutic effects of Xin-II on CHF and investigate the potential molecular pathways underlying these effects using an integrated approach combining network pharmacology and transcriptomic sequencing. METHODS A rat model of CHF was established to assess the therapeutic efficacy of Xin-II. Network pharmacology was used to screen the active components of Xin-II and predict its potential therapeutic targets and key signaling pathways implicated in CHF. Transcriptomic sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed to characterize drug-induced changes in gene expression and further verify the regulatory patterns of candidate signaling pathways identified by network pharmacology. RESULTS Xin-II improved cardiac function and mitigated myocardial pathological lesions in rats with CHF. Transcriptomic analysis and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway enrichment identified the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling pathway as the most significantly enriched pathway, suggesting its potential involvement in the therapeutic effects of Xin-II against CHF. Mechanistically, Xin-II modulated the expression of key genes and proteins associated with the PPAR/hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha signaling cascade. These findings suggest that Xin-II attenuates CHF through multitarget regulation, with the PPAR/hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha axis potentially highlighting an important mechanistic pathway. CONCLUSION This study found that XinII ameliorates CHF through multi-target molecular mechanisms, thereby providing insights into the therapeutic effects of Xin-II and supporting its further investigation as a treatment for CHF. Further, these findings establish a valuable paradigm to advance the modernization and broader application of traditional Mongolian medicine.

title: Umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes ameliorate parathyroid ischemic injury via inhibition of the neutrophil cytosolic factor 4-nuclear factor kappa B pathway
abstractText: BACKGROUND Post-surgical hypoparathyroidism results primarily from mechanical injury to parathyroid tissue or vascular injury during thyroid surgery, leading to glandular ischemia and dysfunction. Patients characteristically exhibit severe hypocalcemia and significantly reduced parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion. The conventional management strategy involves prolonged high-dose supplementation with calcium and active vitamin D. While this approach partially ameliorates hypocalcemia, it cannot substitute for the physiological actions of PTH, especially PTH-mediated calcium reabsorption in the kidney. Therefore, chronic high-dose calcium therapy commonly results in hypercalciuria, substantially elevating the risk of renal dysfunction, kidney stones, and ectopic calcification. Restoration of parathyroid function following surgical injury represents a critical clinical challenge. AIM To investigate the effect of umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (UCMSC-Exo) on rabbit parathyroid injury and to elucidate the mechanism. METHODS We established a rabbit parathyroid ischemia model by ligating the superior thyroid artery branches supplying both parathyroid glands. UCMSC-Exo was injected into the capsule of the parathyroid gland to evaluate the levels of serum PTH and calcium, the histological changes of the parathyroid gland, cell apoptosis and proliferation. Additionally, we studied the effect of UCMSC-Exo on hypoxia-induced damage to rabbit parathyroid cells. Subsequently, rabbit parathyroid tissues were analyzed to elucidate the mechanism by which UCMSC-Exo improves parathyroid injury. RESULTS The results showed that UCMSC-Exo treatment significantly restored PTH and serum calcium levels, alleviated the histological damage of the parathyroid gland, inhibited mitochondrial dysfunction, inhibited cell apoptosis, and promoted cell proliferation. Moreover, in vitro experiments demonstrated that UCMSC-Exo could inhibit the generation of reactive oxygen species in hypoxia-induced parathyroid cells, inhibit cell apoptosis, and promote cell proliferation. Through sequencing and western blot, we found that UCMSC-Exo exerted its protective effect by inhibiting the neutrophil cytosolic factor 4-nuclear factor kappa B signaling pathway. CONCLUSION These findings indicate that local subcapsular injection of UCMSC-Exo has beneficial effects on improving rabbit parathyroid injury and is a promising therapeutic strategy for preventing parathyroid dysfunction after thyroid surgery.

title: Pacing in adults with complex congenital heart disease: A narrative minireview
abstractText: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a growing health care problem, as more pediatric patients survive to adulthood every year as the number of patients with complex conditions also increases. As more patients survive, there has been an increase in the need for pacemaker procedures. Historically, there has been a focus on epicardial pacing in the most complex groups. In this review, we examine the background epidemiology, existing evidence for pacing, extraction data in three of the most complex CHD groups- transposition of the great arteries with an atrial switch procedure, patients palliated with a Fontan procedure and univentricular hearts. In this expert narrative review, we have used a broad search strategy of PubMed supplemented with evidence where available from non-congenital cohorts. The evidence in these most complex cohorts can be limited to expert centre opinion, small numbers and mixed paediatric/adult data. We discuss below the available data, the limitations and the novel approaches available in centres to deal with the most complex conditions such as conduction system pacing and leadless pacing with promising results albeit in expert centres only. Whilst current applicability to a wider range of institutions is not yet suggested by the paper, this review hopefully illustrates potential options for consideration and research in the future.

title: Stem cell-based therapy for premature ovarian insufficiency: From mechanisms to clinical translation
abstractText: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a major cause of diminished fertility and premature reproductive aging. POI is accompanied by vasomotor, physical, psychosocial, and sexual symptoms that substantially affect women’s health and quality of life. Hormone replacement therapy remains the cornerstone of symptomatic management; however, it does not restore ovarian reserve or reproductive potential. Thus, stem cell-based therapies have emerged as novel regenerative strategies, supported by preclinical evidence of improved ovarian function, follicular development, and microenvironmental remodeling. This review critically summarizes current evidence from in vitro studies, animal models, and clinical trials, focusing on mesenchymal stem cells, human amniotic epithelial cells, embryonic stem cells, and induced pluripotent stem cells. Proposed mechanisms include ovarian homing, paracrine signaling, immunomodulation, anti-apoptotic and antioxidant effects, angiogenesis, extracellular vesicle-mediated communication, and the regulation of follicular development. Early clinical studies suggest feasibility and an acceptable short-term safety profile, with preliminary evidence showing improvements in ovarian endocrine function, menstrual recovery, and selected reproductive outcomes. However, evidence remains preliminary, limited and heterogeneous, with substantial challenges related to cell sources, manufacturing, dosing, delivery, mechanisms of action, long-term safety, potency, and clinical endpoints. Future research should prioritize mechanism-guided, standardized strategies and well-designed randomized controlled trials to establish safety and efficacy.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled virtual organoids: Digital-twin frameworks for predictive stem cell biology and precision regenerative medicine
abstractText: Stem cell and organoid technologies have transformed the study of human development, disease, and tissue regeneration, yet their broader scientific and clinical utility remains constrained by experimental variability, limited throughput, destructive endpoint measurements, incomplete longitudinal tracking, and the difficulty of systematically interrogating complex cell-cell and cell-microenvironment interactions. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal single-cell profiling, high-content imaging, biosensing, and mechanistic simulation are creating the foundations for a new computational paradigm: Artificial intelligence-enabled virtual organoids (AIVOs). We define AIVOs as dynamically updated, biologically constrained digital representations of stem cell-derived organoid systems that integrate experimental data with predictive models to simulate cell-state transitions, tissue self-organisation, perturbation responses, and therapeutic outcomes. Rather than static computational replicas, AIVOs are envisioned as executable digital twins in which virtual cells represent cellular interactions underlying emergent tissue properties. Their proposed architecture comprises five linked stages: Longitudinal multimodal observation, dynamic internal-state estimation, executable virtual-cell and hybrid multiscale modelling, prediction and virtual perturbation, and experimental validation with iterative updating. Longitudinal multimodal measurements provide temporally resolved evidence for estimating cellular and tissue states. These states can be represented in hybrid mechanistic and data-driven models to support trajectory prediction and virtual perturbations. However, no complete AIVO satisfying all of these criteria has yet been demonstrated. Available studies instead largely represent enabling technologies or methodological precedents, with only limited evidence for partial or early AIVO prototypes. Potential applications span developmental biology, disease modelling, precision medicine, and regenerative medicine. AIVOs may prospectively support investigation of lineage and tissue patterning, representation of patient-specific heterogeneity and disease dynamics, virtual evaluation of treatment strategies, and optimisation of differentiation, biomaterial, and graft-design parameters. However, the realisation of AIVOs will require substantial methodological and conceptual advances. Key priorities include standardised longitudinal datasets, interpretable modelling, uncertainty quantification, causal validation, multicentre benchmarking, and assessment of transferability across donors, laboratories, and platforms. Regulatory evaluation will also need to distinguish exploratory simulation from clinically actionable prediction and to define evidentiary standards for digital-twin-supported decision-making. AIVOs may thereby shift organoid research towards more predictive, testable, and adaptive modelling across stem cell biology, disease modelling, drug development, and regenerative medicine.

title: Cardiac comorbidity role in the diagnosis of diabetes mellitus using single lead electrocardiogram utilizing machine learning model
abstractText: BACKGROUND Cardiovascular disease alters electrocardiographic morphology and may obscure diabetes-related electrical signatures, yet its effect on electrocardiogram (ECG)-based detection of type 1 and type 2 diabetes is poorly defined. AIM To investigate whether cardiac comorbidity differentially influences machine-learning detection of the two diabetes types from single-lead ECG. METHODS In this study, 2591 observations remained after exclusion of an erroneous age entry and rerunning the analytical pipeline. Twenty-six XGBoost models were evaluated separately for type 1 and type 2 diabetes within subgroups defined by seven cardiac-status criteria. Primary models used 47 single-lead ECG features and five anthropometric variables and were evaluated with five-fold stratified cross-validation. A post hoc seven-predictor sensitivity analysis assessed model complexity. Area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC) uncertainty was estimated using 2000 bootstrap resamples of out-of-fold predictions, and ΔAUC comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Calibration was assessed using Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, reliability plots, and decision-curve analysis. Validation was observation-level because a persistent patient identifier was not available in the analytical export. RESULTS After correction and full rerun, median AUC was 0.693 for type 1 diabetes (range: 0.660-0.804) and 0.661 for type 2 diabetes (range: 0.543-0.716). No cardiac-pathology ΔAUC comparison remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment; the smallest adjusted P value was 0.064. In the reduced seven-predictor sensitivity analysis, AUC was higher than the 52-predictor model in 17 of 26 evaluable subgroup models, with a median descriptive difference of +0.008. Calibration was suboptimal: Across the 26 models, calibration slopes ranged from 0.078 to 0.467 and intercepts from -1.287 to -0.535. Decision-curve analysis showed threshold-dependent net benefit rather than uniform superiority across the evaluated range. CONCLUSION Single-lead ECG combined with anthropometric information showed moderate internal discrimination for recorded diabetes status, but the corrected analysis did not identify a cardiac-pathology subgroup effect that remained significant after multiplicity adjustment. The reduced-feature sensitivity analysis suggested that similar discrimination may be achievable with fewer predictors, whereas calibration remained inadequate for direct interpretation of model outputs as disease probabilities. These findings do not establish a clinically validated screening or rule-out threshold. Patient-grouped validation, independent threshold validation, and external validation remain necessary before clinical implementation.

title: Potential roles of bacterial extracellular vesicles in mesenchymal stem/stromal cell-mediated bone repair
abstractText: The success of bone repair largely depends on mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs); however, under pathological conditions, dysregulation of the osteoimmune microenvironment often impairs MSC function and compromises bone regeneration. Bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are nanoscale membrane-bound structures released by bacteria that carry bioactive components such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids, mediating bacteria-host communication. Emerging evidence suggests that BEVs may participate in bone tissue homeostasis and repair by regulating immune responses, macrophage polarization, bone metabolism, and angiogenesis. Their effects vary with bacterial source: Vesicles derived from probiotic or commensal bacteria often show immunomodulatory and regenerative potential, whereas those derived from pathogenic bacteria may induce inflammatory responses and exacerbate bone resorption. These effects are also influenced by vesicle cargo, engineering status, and disease context. However, current evidence is predominantly preclinical, and no human clinical efficacy evidence for BEV-mediated bone repair was identified in the literature reviewed. Improvements in bone mass or reductions in bone resorption should not be equated with demonstrated fracture or bone-defect regeneration. In this review, we describe the effects of BEVs on MSCs and the osteoimmune microenvironment, summarize their potential mechanisms in bone repair, and discuss recent progress and future translational prospects of BEV-based strategies.

title: Adaptive Temporal-Scale Mamba with Rhythm-Aware Gating for the Classification of Ictal, Interictal, and Normal EEG Segments
abstractText: Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based classification of ictal, interictal, and normal segments is a core building block of automated seizure-monitoring systems. Existing deep models still struggle to jointly optimize sensitivity, specificity, cross-subject generalization, and computational cost. Motivated by the multi-rhythm structure of EEG, this study proposes an Adaptive Temporal-Scale Mamba with Rhythm-Aware Gating (ATSM-RAG) model. A Rhythm-Aware Gating (RAG) unit maps the relative band power of each EEG segment to a scalar gate that interpolates the discretization step (the effective temporal scale) of a Mamba state-space backbone, adapting the temporal receptive field to the input’s spectral state rather than relying on a fixed time constant. ATSM-RAG is evaluated on two public corpora under patient-independent protocols, and we foreground the two evaluations that are free of cross-corpus confounds. First, on the confound-free binary CHB-MIT benchmark (ictal versus interictal, patient-level leave-one-patient-out cross-validation, 22 folds), ATSM-RAG achieves an accuracy of 99.62% ± 0.35%, a sensitivity of 99.10% ± 0.95%, and a specificity of 99.75% ± 0.30%. Second, following the SzCORE recommendations, event-based scoring on all common-montage CHB-MIT recordings (633 files, 930.6[Formula: see text]h, 165 annotated seizures) yields an event-level sensitivity of 90.3% at 2.4 false alarms per 24[Formula: see text]h, with a median detection latency of 12.3[Formula: see text]s. For completeness, the ternary benchmark (288 ictal and 1440 interictal CHB-MIT segments plus 720 normal segments drawn from clinically normal recordings of the TUH Abnormal EEG Corpus) yields an accuracy of 99.51% ± 0.37%, a sensitivity (ictal recall) of 98.99% ± 1.29%, and a specificity (correct-classification rate of the merged nonictal classes) of 99.58% ± 0.39%. On the TUH EEG Seizure Corpus (official patient-disjoint train/development/evaluation split), ATSM-RAG achieves a binary segment classification accuracy of 97.94%. Ablation experiments show that removing the RAG unit and fixing the temporal scale reduce accuracy by 2.94% and 2.05%, respectively. These results indicate that rhythm-conditioned temporal scaling is a promising and computationally efficient inductive bias for EEG segment classification; prospective and multi-center clinical validation is still required before any clinical deployment.

title: Diagnostic clue in disguise - steroid-aggravated paraparesis revealing spinal perimedullary arteriovenous fistula: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Spinal cord perimedullary arteriovenous fistula (PMAVF) in adults is a rare entity that is often misdiagnosed due to its nonspecific presentation. It mimics lumbar degenerative disease, peripheral neuropathy, or myelopathy. CASE SUMMARY We report a 52-year-old man with a five-year history of symptoms and a prior history of two lumbar spine surgeries for compressive myelopathy due to lumbar disc disease; one-year post-surgery, he developed an asymmetric, progressive paraparesis with sensory and bladder involvement. Magnetic resonance imaging suggested a long-segment cord hyperintensity, and tests for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder were negative. Administration of high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone produced a striking but transient paradoxical worsening of his paraparesis, resolving spontaneously within 36 hours. This atypical steroid-related deterioration prompted reconsideration of the diagnosis, and spinal digital subtraction angiography confirmed a PMAVF at the L3–L4 level fed by a radiculomedullary branch of the left T9 intercostal artery. CONCLUSION This case illustrates the pitfall of diagnosing venous congestive myelopathy as compressive myelopathy; also, acute clinical worsening following steroid administration in a patient is a diagnostic clue to an underlying spinal cord arteriovenous fistula.

title: Severe Hageman factor (factor XII) deficiency discovered during evaluation of palpitations and chest pain: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Factor XII (FXII), or Hageman factor, deficiency is a rare, usually autosomal recessive, defect of the contact pathway of coagulation. It characteristically causes a markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) with a normal prothrombin time (PT) and no bleeding tendency, and it is usually discovered incidentally on preoperative or routine screening. Whether FXII deficiency has any clinical consequence, including thrombosis, remains debated, and reports of symptomatic patients usually involve a confirmed thrombotic event. CASE SUMMARY A 36-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B on antiviral therapy, hyperlipidemia and prediabetes presented to the emergency department after two brief episodes, on separate days, of palpitations, mild (2/10) burning left-sided chest pain and shortness of breath; his smartwatch recorded a heart rate of 118 beats per minute during one episode. The symptoms had resolved on arrival. Vital signs, troponin, chest radiograph and electrocardiogram (sinus rhythm with possible right ventricular hypertrophy) showed no acute abnormality. The APTT was > 400 seconds on two measurements with a normal PT and international normalized ratio. A mixing study corrected the APTT, favoring a factor deficiency over an inhibitor, and antiphospholipid testing was normal. FXII activity was < 1% on repeat testing, whereas factors IX and XI, high-molecular-weight kininogen, prekallikrein and von Willebrand parameters were normal. Severe FXII deficiency was diagnosed. No bleeding or thrombosis occurred, symptoms did not recur during telemetry observation, and no treatment was required. The patient was discharged with hematology follow-up and a recommendation for family testing. CONCLUSION In this patient, severe FXII deficiency was an incidental finding and is not considered the cause of the transient symptoms, which remained unexplained. A markedly prolonged isolated APTT warrants a systematic evaluation with mixing studies and factor assays, but the result must be interpreted in the full clinical context, and the patient's symptoms should be evaluated independently rather than attributed prematurely to the laboratory abnormality.

title: Is somatosensory tinnitus confined to the craniocervical region: Diagnostic pitfalls, manual therapy and safety considerations
abstractText: Somatosensory tinnitus is tinnitus that is triggered or modulated by somatic input, and current diagnostic criteria locate that input in the cervical spine and temporomandibular region. This minireview, based on a structured narrative search of PubMed (January 2015 to October 2026), grades the evidence for somatic modulation by body region and examines diagnosis, conservative management and safety. Evidence is strongest for the jaw, face and neck, where auditory-somatosensory convergence in the dorsal cochlear nucleus is anatomically established and small randomized trials of cervical and temporomandibular manual therapy report short-term benefit with a high risk of bias. Modulation by limb contractions is documented but preliminary. Evidence for a lumbosacral contribution is indirect, consisting of confounded spinal neuromodulation case reports, a cross-sectional association with low back pain and uncontrolled observations; no anatomical projection has been demonstrated, and no controlled study has tested lumbar-directed treatment for tinnitus. One author-managed patient, whose tinnitus began with acute lumbosacral pain during use of a percussive massage device, is used only to frame four diagnostic pitfalls; this uncontrolled observation cannot establish causation, a lumbosacral mechanism or a treatment effect, and no recommendation depends on it. We compare manual therapy with guidelines that recommend cognitive behavioural therapy, summarise published massage-device adverse events, which are case reports that cannot establish causation or incidence, outline practical suicide screening tools and recommend validated outcome measures. An expanded somatic examination can be considered when specific history clues are present, but its yield is unknown, and we define research priorities to test it.

title: System dynamics modeling for performance optimization in a pipe manufacturing system: An ethiopian case analysis
abstractText: This study presents a system dynamics-based case study aimed at evaluating and enhancing the performance of a manufacturing system, with specific application to the Amhara Pipe Factory in Ethiopia. Manufacturing systems in developing economies often face challenges related to capacity utilization, operational inefficiencies, and human performance, which collectively limit their ability to meet customer demand and maintain competitiveness. To address these issues, a system dynamics model integrating human factors, process factors, and product and service factors was developed using empirical data collected through questionnaires, interviews, direct observations, and company records. Statistical analysis using IBM SPSS was applied to identify and prioritize key performance-influencing factors, which were subsequently incorporated into the simulation model developed in Vensim software. Three policy scenarios were evaluated to assess potential performance improvements: variation in customer demand, reduction of cycle time and downtime, and enhancement of employee training and experience. Simulation results indicate that increasing customer demand by 50% improves production performance by 0.457%, while reducing cycle time and downtime by 50% increases performance by 2.257%. The most significant improvement was observed under the human-factor-focused scenario, where enhancing employee training and experience by 50% resulted in a 26.6% increase in production performance, achieving up to 98.1% of the desired production capacity. Unlike conventional static performance assessment approaches, the proposed framework captures the dynamic interactions and feedback relationships among manufacturing system variables, enabling long-term evaluation of alternative operational policies. The findings highlight the critical role of human factors in manufacturing system performance and demonstrate the usefulness of system dynamics modeling as a decision-support tool for performance improvement in industrial and environmental engineering applications.

Phlebolith-rich axillary venous malformation masquerading as lymphadenopathy of a multimodal diagnostic pitfall: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Venous malformations (VMs) are predominantly slow-flow vascular anomalies in which recurrent thrombosis can result in phlebolith formation. Deep axillary lesions may resemble lymphadenopathy, particularly when Doppler flow is minimal or undetectable in the interrogated component. CASE SUMMARY A phlebolith-rich axillary VM mimicking lymphadenopathy in a 39-year-old woman: Clustered calcifications with minimal Doppler flow prompted vascular reassessment before excision. CONCLUSION Clustered rounded calcifications, acoustic shadowing despite minimal regional Doppler flow, extension beyond a single nodal station and nondiagnostic blood-containing sampling should prompt consideration of a vascular anomaly. Targeted vascular imaging and assessment of venous connections may improve pre-intervention planning.

Proliferative spasmolytic polypeptide-expressing metaplasia in gastric carcinogenesis: Stem cell origins, lineage plasticity, and clinical implications
abstractText: Spasmolytic polypeptide-expressing metaplasia (SPEM) is a common, biologically heterogeneous metaplastic phenotype arising in the gastric corpus after oxyntic gland injury. Acute injury-associated SPEM is usually transient and reversible, whereas persistent inflammatory or oncogenic stimulation can result in SPEM with sustained proliferative activity, intestinal differentiation, incomplete intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and molecular alterations associated with neoplastic progression. These features identify proliferative SPEM as a progression-associated subset with greater relevance to gastric carcinogenesis. The cellular origin of SPEM remains unresolved and varies among experimental models. Lineage-tracing studies support contributions from corpus isthmus stem/progenitor cells, chief-cell-labeled populations, and the mucous neck-chief transitional lineage. Most of the related lineage-tracing and mechanistic evidence has been derived using mouse models, whereas clinicopathological and molecular associations have been primarily demonstrated via human studies. SPEM is not an obligatory intermediate in gastric carcinogenesis, and its neoplastic potential is linked to particular proliferative metaplastic populations and accompanying stem/progenitor-cell alterations. Reproducible pathological and molecular criteria and prospective human validation are required to establish the value of proliferative SPEM for risk stratification and surveillance.

title: Restoration of inflammatory responsiveness by metformin in endothelial cells derived from Marfan syndrome patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cells
abstractText: BACKGROUND Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a hereditary connective tissue disorder that considerably increases the risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. Endothelial cell (EC) dysfunction is now widely regarded as a key contributor to the vascular pathology associated with MFS. AIM To characterize endothelial dysfunction in patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived ECs (MFS-iECs) from patients with MFS and to determine whether metformin and resveratrol can ameliorate these abnormalities. METHODS MFS-induced pluripotent stem cells were reprogrammed from patient-derived cells and differentiated into ECs. EC proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, nitric oxide bioavailability, cellular senescence, and mitochondrial function were evaluated in MFS-iECs and wild-type iECs. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to characterize inflammatory signaling and responses to TNF-α stimulation. MFS-iECs were subsequently treated with metformin or resveratrol to assess their effects on endothelial inflammatory phenotypes. RESULTS Compared with wild-type-iECs, MFS-iECs exhibited impaired proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, and nitric oxide bioavailability, as well as accelerated cellular senescence and mitochondrial dysfunction. Transcriptomic analysis revealed hyperactivated inflammatory signaling, blunted responsiveness to TNF-α stimulation, and enhanced NF-κB pathway activity. Metformin partially restored inflammatory responsiveness to TNF-α in MFS-iECs without significantly altering basal inflammation or cellular senescence, whereas resveratrol dose-dependently suppressed basal proinflammatory cytokine expression. CONCLUSION These findings reveal profound endothelial dysfunction and inflammatory dysregulation in human MFS-iECs. Metformin and resveratrol modulate endothelial inflammation through distinct mechanisms, providing a novel translational basis for developing EC-targeted therapies in patients with MFS.

title: Stem cell preconditioning for enhanced therapeutic efficacy: Translational challenges and strategic solutions
abstractText: Stem cell preconditioning can enhance survival, trafficking, and paracrine activity, but promising preclinical enhancement has not yet translated into a comparably mature clinical evidence base. To evaluate the product development requirements for preconditioned stem cells and their extracellular vesicles (EVs) products, we propose a pharmaceutical product development framework, and identify priorities for future translational research. We integrated a comparative assessment of major preconditioning strategies and an analysis of registered clinical trials with product development principles. We also examined their derivative EV products derived from preconditioned stem cells and potential applications of artificial intelligence. The registry analysis identified a small, heterogeneous clinical landscape dominated by early-phase trials and limited use of matched unpreconditioned comparators, restricting assessment of the incremental contribution of preconditioning. We proposed a product lifecycle framework linking the quality target product profile to mechanism of action, critical quality attributes, potency assays, process standardization, good manufacturing practice manufacturing, scale-up, comparability, and risk management. For EV products, preconditioned source cell constitutes an upstream process variable, while the administered product requires specific characterization and potency assessment. Priorities included combined preconditioning methods, transparent reporting and validation of artificial intelligence approaches for optimization and monitoring. Stem cell preconditioning should be developed as a controlled manufacturing step, with quality and potency requirements tailored to the product and indication. This framework may guide the development of reproducible, scalable stem cells and EV products, while clinical studies with appropriate comparators remain necessary to establish the added therapeutic value of preconditioning.

title: FRACTAL-FRACTIONAL DIABETES MELLITUS MODEL WITHOUT GENETIC INFLUENCES: NUMERICAL INVESTIGATIONS
abstractText: In this study, we present an accurate simulation to examine the behavior of solutions to the mathematical model of diabetes without genetic factors (MMDWGF) in its fractal-fractional form. To accomplish this goal, we provide a potential approximation method based on Appell-type Changhee polynomials (ACPs). We employ the spectral collocation method (SCM) in accordance with the characteristics of the ACPs. The proposed technique transforms the given model into a nonlinear system of algebraic equations. The use of Picard’s theorem to investigate the critical points of the model, the existence of the solution, and originality is given special attention. The outcomes generated by the RK4 method and the ones acquired visually exhibit similarities. We also compared the results of the given method with the numerical scheme that was previously published, where we computed the residual error function with different values of the approximation-order, to estimate the effectiveness and precision of the proposed methodology. Based on our findings, the technique used offers a helpful tool for simulating the solution of these systems. One of the main advantages of the proposed method is that it requires only a few easy steps, does not generate secular boundaries, and does not require a disturbance parameter.

title: Tool Replacement Policy for Degrading Processes with Asymmetric Specification Limits
abstractText: In manufacturing industries, tool wear seems to be the most general cause behind gradual degradation of a process over time. Therefore, a systematic tool monitoring and replacement policy is the need of the hour for them. Although, a considerable amount of research work has already been done to address this issue, they primarily focus on quality characteristics having symmetric bilateral specification limits. However, in practice, often such symmetry, with respect to the target, is violated due to several practical reasons. This issue has been addressed in this paper by defining a process capability index (PCI) for degrading processes having asymmetric specification limits. Some mathematical formulations have also been suggested, based on the concepts of threshold value and maximum allowable nonconformance probability, to decide about the tool changing time, in an objective way. These should be of particular interest to production managers in taking strategic decisions regarding tool replacement. A Monte Carlo simulation study and a numerical example have also been discussed to supplement the theory developed in this paper.

However, the chemical effects of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes, including their long-term consequences, remain poorly explored. This study aims to characterize the chemical impact of a luminosity outburst on the envelope of a solar-type protostar, considering the dynamics of the system, and identify trends in the molecular response relative to both ongoing and past outburst activity. title: Familial cryptorchidism in three siblings: Three case reports
abstractText: BACKGROUND Cryptorchidism, or undescended testis, is the most common congenital anomaly of the male genitalia. Although most cases are considered multifactorial, familial clustering suggests an important heritable component, while rare monogenic forms involving genes regulating testicular descent have also been described. CASE SUMMARY We report three brothers aged 8, 10, and 12 years, each presenting with unilateral cryptorchidism. The youngest child had a palpable left inguinal testicular remnant and underwent inguinal exploration, which revealed a markedly atrophic testicular nubbin; orchiectomy was performed. The two older brothers had non-palpable testes. Magnetic resonance imaging suggested intra-abdominal locations near the external iliac vessels, and diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed markedly hypoplastic testes near the deep inguinal rings. Laparoscopic orchiectomy was performed in both patients. All three patients had normally descended contralateral testes and an uneventful postoperative recovery. CONCLUSION The occurrence of cryptorchidism in multiple siblings should prompt careful family history-taking and examination of male siblings. Recognition of familial clustering may facilitate earlier diagnosis and management. Further genetic studies are required to determine whether apparently isolated familial clusters represent multifactorial susceptibility or rare monogenic disorders.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Science and Physics Education, 2015-2026: An AI-Assisted Bibliometric and Title-and-Abstract Analysis across Fourteen Journals
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) research in science and physics education has expanded rapidly, particularly since the emergence of generative AI. This study maps publication patterns, research characteristics, and citation connections across 14 selected science and physics education journals. OpenAlex searches using fifteen AI-related terms identified 966 unique records published between January 2015 and September 2026. AI-assisted screening retained 333 publications, which were coded using available titles and abstracts. Bibliometric analyses examined publication growth, thematic patterns, and citations within and between the two journal groups. Of the included publications, 87.1% appeared from 2023 onwards. Generative large language models and chatbots accounted for 58.9% of the corpus, while instruction and assessment together represented 48.3% of publications. Among 182 records classified as involving human participants, comparison groups were identifiable in 14.3%, effect sizes in 8.2%, and instrument validity evidence in 5.5%. These frequencies reflect information identifiable in bibliographic records, rather than the absence of these features in the full studies. Laboratory and experimental support was the principal educational function in 27 publications. Citation connections between the journal groups were limited: their reference sets had a Jaccard index of 0.047, and 15.6% of publications cited an included study from the other group. The findings document rapid growth and uneven research emphases within the selected venues. Independent human validation and full-text assessment are needed before drawing firm conclusions about methodological quality or educational effectiveness.

title: Apparent palatal root separation in a maxillary second molar: A case report and review of literature
abstractText: BACKGROUND Maxillary second molars usually have one palatal root. Two independent palatal roots are uncommon and can be overlooked when two-dimensional radiographs superimpose the roots. CASE SUMMARY A 26-year-old man presented with spontaneous and lingering thermal pain associated with the maxillary left second molar. Clinical findings supported a diagnosis of symptomatic irreversible pulpitis. After access under rubber dam isolation, examination with a dental operating microscope identified four canal orifices: Mesiobuccal, distobuccal, mesiopalatal, and distopalatal. Management and outcome: The four canals were prepared with nickel-titanium rotary instruments, irrigated with sodium hypochlorite and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, and obturated with gutta-percha and a bioceramic sealer. Selected post-obturation cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images suggested apparent palatal root separation at the displayed levels. The original Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine volume, acquisition information, clinical indication, and formal interpretation were unavailable; complete independence of the palatal roots could not be confirmed. Three-month follow-up was clinically favorable, but the absence of diagnostic-quality baseline and paired follow-up periapical radiographs prevented assessment of baseline apical status and radiographic healing. Incomplete procedural records also limited assessment of treatment quality and reproducibility. Review synthesis: A focused narrative review distinguishes external root separation from multiple canals within one palatal root and emphasizes anatomical recognition, selective imaging, and procedural documentation. Study-specific frequencies cannot be pooled because populations, methods, and definitions differ. Four orifices do not establish four independent roots, and selected postoperative images do not substitute for serial multiplanar assessment. CONCLUSION Two palatal orifices should prompt assessment for complex internal anatomy or separate palatal roots. In this case, magnified inspection supported canal identification, while the available images suggested palatal root separation without establishing complete independence. The outcome represents favorable early clinical follow-up at 3 months. CBCT requires an individual clinical justification; this report does not establish an indication for routine postoperative scanning.

title: Promoter-proximal chromatin accessibility is associated with restricted developmental competence of somatic cell nuclear transfer-derived trophoblast stem cells
abstractText: BACKGROUND Somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) restores totipotency to a differentiated genome; however, cloned mammals exhibit low efficiency and frequently display placental overgrowth, indicating that the reprogramming of the extraembryonic lineage may be less faithful than that of the embryonic lineage. While nuclear transfer embryonic stem cells are comparable to normal cells, cloned placentas consistently present abnormalities. Available evidence derives from terminal tissues, making it challenging to distinguish primary defects from secondary consequences. Whether this deficiency is intrinsic to the trophoblast compartment and whether it is heritable in a self-renewing state remain unresolved. AIM To determine whether cloned trophoblast harbors an intrinsic, heritable reprogramming defect and to define its chromatin basis. METHODS Nuclear transfer trophoblast stem cells (ntTSCs) and fertilization-derived trophoblast stem cells (TSCs) were derived concurrently from mouse SCNT blastocysts reconstructed with cumulus cell nuclei and from in vitro fertilization-derived blastocysts, respectively; independently derived lines per group, passage-matched at passage 10, were utilized in all experiments. Karyotyping, marker expression, immunofluorescence, and in vitro differentiation assessed the lines. mCherry-labelled cells were injected into 8-cell embryos to quantify placental chimerism and into SCNT 8-cell embryos for complementation tests; embryos were transferred to pseudopregnant recipients across three prospectively planned groups and conceptuses were recovered at embryonic day 18.5. Assays for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (two biological replicates per cell type) and RNA sequencing (three biological replicates per cell type) were integrated, alongside reanalysis of published TEAD4 and TFAP2C chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) data generated in fertilization-derived TSCs; transcription factor occupancy was therefore inferred from public data and was not measured in ntTSCs. RESULTS ntTSCs were euploid, self-renewed with epithelial morphology, expressed a canonical trophoblast program (Cdx2, Eomes, Elf5, Gata3, Fgfr2, Esrrb, Sox2) devoid of pluripotency genes, and demonstrated in vitro differentiation. Despite maintaining this identity, ntTSCs colonized the placenta less efficiently than TSCs, failed to improve the implantation rate of SCNT embryos, unlike TSC supplementation, which significantly improved the rate, though not to levels observed with in vitro fertilization levels, and produced hypertrophic placentas with reduced labyrinth area and dysregulated imprinting. Accessibility reprogramming was largely complete, with only approximately 4% of differential regions remaining resistant. Of these, 224 somatic-type regions did not close, were primarily promoter-proximal, and enriched for activator protein 1 (AP-1)/JunB motifs, while 403 trophoblast-type regions did not open, carrying TEAD4 and TFAP2C motifs but displaying lower occupancy in published TSC ChIP-seq data, remaining silent, including Nr0b1 and Prdm10. CONCLUSION A small, promoter-proximal fraction of the epigenome resists SCNT reprogramming. This residual, incompletely switched AP-1-to-TEAD4/TFAP2C signature is stably propagated through self-renewal and is associated with, though not yet proven to cause, the limited developmental competence of cloned trophoblast.

title: Explant isolation and regional heterogeneity of mesenchymal stromal/stem cell-related cells from rat digestive-tract segments: Preclinical electroacupuncture basis for low anterior resection syndrome
abstractText: BACKGROUND The functions of mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (MSCs) can be influenced by tissue origin and local microenvironment; however, comparative studies of cells derived from proximal-to-distal segments of the same digestive tract remain limited. AIM To compare the in vitro phenotype, proliferation, and tri-lineage induction staining responses of cells derived from proximal-to-distal segments of the rat esophagus, stomach, and jejunum, and to evaluate their regional functional heterogeneity. METHODS Esophageal, gastric, and jejunal tissues were obtained from 6-week-old male Sprague-Dawley rats. Under a stereomicroscope, the mucosal layer was carefully removed from all three tissues, and the submucosa and muscularis were retained. Cells were isolated and cultured using the tissue explant adherence method, and primary outgrowth and proliferation were recorded. Flow cytometry was used to detect CD90, CD73, CD44, CD34, CD45, and CD11b/c. Osteogenic, adipogenic, and chondrogenic induction was performed, followed by staining and image-based semi-quantification. Independent animals were used as biological replicates, with n = 4 per group. RESULTS All three cell populations highly expressed CD90, CD73, and CD44 and had low CD34 and CD45 expression. CD11b/c was generally low but showed regional differences. Esophageal cells generally showed higher CD90, CD73, and CD44 expression, whereas jejunal cells showed higher CD11b/c expression (6.05% ± 0.91%) than esophageal (3.01% ± 0.53%) and gastric (2.37% ± 0.50%) cells. CD34 and CD45 were low in all three groups; jejunal CD45 was 5.08% ± 0.79%. Esophageal cells showed faster primary outgrowth and proliferation and stronger osteogenic staining; jejunal cells showed higher adipogenic staining; chondrogenic staining did not differ significantly among groups. Tri-lineage induction staining results were mainly based on semi-quantitative staining analysis and should not be interpreted as complete lineage commitment. CONCLUSION Cells from different segments of the digestive tract show regional differences in phenotype, proliferation, and osteogenic/adipogenic induction staining responses, whereas chondrogenic staining does not differ significantly. At this stage, these cells should be described as cell populations with MSC-related phenotypes. Their mechanisms and therapeutic value require further molecular and in vivo validation.

title: Transvaginal small bowel evisceration twenty-two years after laparoscopic hysterectomy: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Vaginal cuff dehiscence associated with bowel evisceration is an uncommon condition. Very late presentation after hysterectomy can delay recognition because the original surgery may be overlooked. CASE SUMMARY An 84-year-old woman developed sudden transvaginal protrusion of the small bowel, severe abdominal pain, and urinary retention after 3 days of diarrhea and urinary symptoms. She had undergone total laparoscopic hysterectomy 22 years earlier. Examination revealed bowel congestion at the vaginal opening. Emergency laparotomy confirmed evisceration through the vaginal cuff defect with friable edges. A 50-cm ileal segment was herniated through the cuff. The compromised bowel was resected. The short, viable distal ileal remnant required right hemicolectomy and ileo-ascending anastomosis. The cuff was closed transabdominally in two layers. Early postoperative rigors and vomiting were managed with nasogastric decompression and antibiotics. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 8. Further documented follow-up data were not available. CONCLUSION Remote hysterectomy does not exclude the possibility of cuff dehiscence. Visible transvaginal bowel requires urgent surgical assessment and individualized management.

title: Giant goiter in a patient with Graves’ disease and severe elephantiasic pretibial myxedema: A case report and review of literature
abstractText: BACKGROUND Giant goiter in Graves’ disease (GD) is an uncommon clinical presentation that may cause substantial compressive symptoms and complicate disease management. Elephantiasic pretibial myxedema (PTM) is a rare and severe extrathyroidal manifestation of GD, and its clinical course may not parallel changes in thyroid function. The coexistence of these conditions presents considerable therapeutic challenges. CASE SUMMARY A 49-year-old man with a 26-year history of GD presented with progressive thyroid enlargement, refractory hyperthyroidism, and severe bilateral elephantiasic PTM. The massive goiter caused marked neck swelling and dyspnea in the supine position, substantially impairing his quality of life. Following comprehensive preoperative medical optimization, the patient successfully underwent total thyroidectomy. The resected thyroid gland weighed 544 g, with an estimated volume of 445.6 mL based on three-dimensional computed tomography reconstruction. Histopathological examination revealed nodular goiter with adenomatous hyperplastic nodules. At the 1-year follow-up, thyroid function showed an overall trend toward stability under levothyroxine replacement therapy, with no evidence of recurrent hyperthyroidism and complete resolution of compressive neck symptoms. However, bilateral elephantiasic PTM showed no meaningful improvement and appeared to progress during follow-up. In addition, serum thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibody levels remained markedly elevated (> 40 IU/L) 12 months after thyroidectomy. We also reviewed the available literature on the management of giant goiter in GD and PTM to provide a broader clinical context for this case. CONCLUSION This case highlights the challenges of managing giant goiter in GD complicated by severe elephantiasic PTM. The persistence and apparent progression of PTM despite thyroidectomy and postoperative improvement in thyroid function suggest that the cutaneous manifestations may follow a clinical course partly independent of thyroid hormone status. Persistent autoimmune activity and potentially irreversible tissue remodeling may contribute to this phenomenon, although further investigation is needed. Long-term monitoring of PTM should therefore be considered even after definitive treatment of GD.

title: Kajian Kriminogen Tindak Pidana Narkotika Yang Dilakukan oleh Anak
abstractText: Pasal 1 angka 1 Undang-undang Nomor 35 Tahun 2009 tentang Narkotika menyatakan akibat dari penyalahgunaan narkotika. Berdasarkan Pasal 2 Undang-undang Nomor 11 Tahun 2012 tentang Sistem Peradilan Pidana Anak, penanganan anak yang berkonflik dengan hukum harus mengutamakan prinsip perlindungan, rehabilitasi, dan pemulihan sosial. Keterlibatan anak-anak dalam tindak pidana narkotika dapat dijelaskan melalui teori faktor kriminogen. Faktor kriminogen adalah elemen-elemen yang memicu atau mendorong seseorang untuk melakukan kejahatan. Kajian penelitian ini adalah tentang faktor kriminogen terjadinya tindak pidana narkotika yang dilakukan oleh anak di wilayah hukum Polresta Padang serta upaya mengurangi faktor kriminogen pada tindak pidana narkotika yang dilakukan oleh anak. Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian hukum dengan spesifikasi yang bersifat deskriptif analitis. Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah pendekatan Yuridis Normatif yang didukung pendekatan Yuridis Empiris. Hasil penelitian diperoleh faktor kriminogen terjadinya tindak pidana narkotika yang dilakukan oleh anak di Wilayah Hukum Polresta Padang yaitu: 1) bergaul dalam lingkungan yang telah terbiasa dengan aktivitas peredaran narkotika, 2) Lingkungan yang memiliki tingkat kejahatan tinggi sering kali menjadi tempat berkembangnya berbagai aktivitas ilegal, termasuk peredaran narkotika, 3) kondisi keluarga yang tidak harmonis, 4) tekanan dari kelompok sebaya, 5) faktor ekonomi, 6) Sekolah yang gagal dalam memberikan pengawasan yang cukup terhadap murid-muridnya, sehingga anak-anak yang mulai mencoba menggunakan narkotika tidak mendapatkan bimbingan atau intervensi yang tepat. Upaya mengurangi faktor kriminogen adalah dengan melaksanakan berbagai program penyuluhan dan sosialisasi di sekolah-sekolah untuk meningkatkan kesadaran para siswa mengenai bahaya narkotika, dengan melibatkan pihak sekolah, Badan Narkotika Nasional (BNN), serta berbagai instansi terkait yang memiliki pengalaman dalam menangani kasus penyalahgunaan narkotika di kalangan anak-anak dan remaja juga orang yang pernah menggunakan narkotika.

The solitudes of the caesarean section: A family medicine perspective using Gibbs’ Reflective Cycle
abstractText: For this structured reflection, I consider my experiences from interviews with mothers undergoing caesarean sections (C-sections) at two government hospitals. I reflect on their lonely journey and how it aligns with the principles of family medicine in improving the process of giving birth. During my data collection, only one out of the 60 patients I interviewed was visited by her partner before and after the C-section, which made me uneasy for all other women who were left alone during this critical time in their lives. For vaginal deliveries, there exists a guideline for companionship during labour, which has positive emotional and physical outcomes. However, no such guideline has been developed for the C-section. Contribution: The successful birth of a child and the time that follows it are widely defined by the support of family and community. As such, I propose that the mothers undergoing elective C-sections should receive treatment based on the principles of family medicine.

title: Grade 4 reading comprehension in South Africa: Evidence from a 4-year repeated cross-sectional study in Makhanda, South Africa
abstractText: Background: South Africa’s literacy crisis is well documented nationally, but repeated local evidence on Grade 4 reading outcomes remains limited. Objectives: The study examined Grade 4 reading comprehension and oral reading fluency (ORF) across successive cohorts in Makhanda, considering school socioeconomic context and Language of Learning and Teaching (LOLT). Method: A repeated cross-sectional study assessed 4306 learners in 25 primary schools from 2023 to 2026. Comprehension was assessed in the Foundation Phase LOLT using a 24-mark instrument, with 15/24 as a study-defined benchmark. ORF was assessed in a stratified subsample. As testing took place in October 2023 but February thereafter, direct comparisons focused on 2024–2026. Results: Across four cohorts, 37%–45% met the comprehension benchmark. Among the comparable 2024–2026 cohorts, attainment varied by school quintile and LOLT. Within Quintile 3, learners in three English LOLT schools achieved higher benchmark attainment than those in nine isiXhosa LOLT schools, although schools varied within each group. ORF was strongly associated with comprehension in both language groups. Conclusion: Persistent inequalities in Grade 4 reading outcomes were associated with socioeconomic and language contexts. Learners in English LOLT schools consistently achieved higher comprehension outcomes than those in isiXhosa LOLT schools, including within the same quintile. These patterns highlight the importance of language pathways and their implementation conditions. Contribution: Four years of locality-level evidence show how sustained local assessment can reveal literacy inequalities obscured by national averages and inform contextually responsive research, planning and support.

title: Interventions to improve physical activity and health outcomes among adolescents in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review protocol
abstractText: Background: Global adolescent populations fall short of meeting the recommended levels of physical activity associated with achieving health benefits. Considering the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) within sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), implementing contextually relevant physical activity interventions among adolescents may help improve health outcomes, thereby curbing future increases in the disease burden. Despite low research productivity on such topics, the extent of the available literature within SSA is yet to be investigated. Aim: This review aims to summarise the available evidence on physical activity interventions implemented among adolescents in SSA to promote physical activity and improve health outcomes. Setting: Sub-Saharan Africa. Methods: A scoping review will be conducted following Arksey and O’Malley’s framework and the Joana Briggs Institute guidelines. Systematic searches for eligible articles will be conducted across six electronic databases, namely EBSCOhost, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Sabinet African Journals, Web of Science and PubMed between 2004 and 2025. The search process will be recorded on a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses flow chart. Results: Data from the selected articles will be extracted and charted using a prepiloted data extraction sheet. Study findings will be analysed descriptively and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Conclusion: This protocol outlines the study’s rationale, objectives and methodology considerations. A scoping review will provide an overview of available research and highlight knowledge gaps. Contribution: This synthesis will offer valuable insights to researchers and physical activity promotion planners, informing future policy and practices.

title: Helicobacter pylori Test Positivity and Associated Factors among Laboratory-Tested Patients in Duhok Governorate, Iraq: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstractText: Background: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is one of the most common chronic bacterial infections worldwide and is associated with several gastrointestinal disorders. Monitoring its prevalence is important for disease control and healthcare planning. Objectives: To determine the distribution of H. pylori test positivity among laboratory-tested patients in Duhok Governorate and to evaluate its association with demographic characteristics, diagnostic method, and month of testing during 2025. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using records of patients tested for H. pylori at three laboratories in Duhok Governorate, Iraq, between January and December 2025 Data on age, gender, diagnostic method, testing month, and test results were analyzed using SPSS version 25. Results: Among 1,222 patients, 58.3% were female, with a mean age of 34.46 ± 17.48 years. Of the 1,222 patients, 399 tested positive, corresponding to an overall positivity rate of 32.7%. H. pylori infection was significantly associated with age group (p = 0.002), testing month (p < 0.001), and diagnostic method (p < 0.001). The highest numbers of positive cases were observed in the 20–29 and 30–39 year age groups and during July and November. Gender was not significantly associated with test positivity (p = 0.761). Conclusion: H. pylori test positivity was observed among patients undergoing laboratory testing in Duhok Governorate. Age group and diagnostic method were significantly associated with test positivity, whereas gender was not. Monthly differences should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial variation in testing volume.

title: Ophthalmology referral patterns at a tertiary service before, during and after COVID-19
abstractText: Background: The Vula Medical digital referral platform connected South African primary-care providers with specialist services. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic disrupted routine healthcare delivery and may have altered referral patterns. This study examined changes in ophthalmology referrals to a tertiary South African hospital submitted via Vula Medical across pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic periods. Methods: Retrospective comparative descriptive analysis of anonymised referral data for July 2018, July 2020 and July 2025. All ophthalmology referrals submitted via Vula Medical to Tygerberg Hospital were included, excluding duplicate, test or incomplete entries. Referral volume, urgency, diagnostic category and specialist response were compared across periods. Results: A total of 1498 referrals were analysed. Referral volume fell by 46.5% in July 2020 compared with July 2018 and rose to 107% above baseline by July 2025. Urgent referrals increased from 34.0% (2018) to 49.1% (2020) and declined to 21.7% (2025). Cataract referrals fell to 5.4% during the pandemic and became the leading reason for referral (21.5%) by 2025. Advice-only management rose to 42.8% during the pandemic. Conclusion: COVID-19 was associated with substantial changes in ophthalmology referral patterns. The digital referral platform facilitated remote triage during disruption and structured prioritisation during recovery, supporting a role for digital referral systems in resilient specialist care. Contribution: This study contributes longitudinal evidence on the role of digital referral platforms in maintaining specialist ophthalmology access during health-system disruption, informing referral-pathway design and capacity planning for African health systems within the scope of the JCMSA.
