title: Gendered risks in mining: Health and safety challenges faced by women in South Africa’s platinum industry
abstractText: Orientation: Legislative reforms have been introduced in South Africa to promote gender equality and improve working conditions in the mining sector; however, occupational environments remain structured around male-oriented norms and practices. As a result, women continue to face gender-specific risks which remain insufficiently addressed. Research purpose: The aim of the study was to investigate the health and safety challenges faced by women employed in South Africa’s platinum mining industry. Motivation for the study: There is a need for empirical, context-specific evidence to better understand and address gendered health and safety risks and to inform effective interventions in mining organisations. Research approach/design and method: The study adopted a cross-sectional exploratory research design and a quantitative research approach. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire distributed to women employed in mining operations at a platinum mine in South Africa. An availability sampling was used to select the respondents, resulting in 196 completed responses. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multivariate analyses. Main findings: The findings indicate that gender-specific health and safety risks, including physical and ergonomic mismatches, inadequate PPE fit, deficient ablution and sanitation infrastructure and experiences of discrimination and sexual harassment in the mining workplace remain insufficiently addressed, highlighting gaps in the protection and inclusion of women. Practical/managerial implications: The study offers practical recommendations that mining organisations can implement to address structural, occupational and psychosocial safety challenges, thereby improving women’s workplace experiences and advancing gender transformation in the South African mining industry. Contribution/value-add: The study provides empirical insights into gendered health and safety risks experienced by women in platinum mining and offers empirical evidence to inform on gender-responsive organisational interventions, workplace policies and human resources management practices.

title: Effect of Habitat Type on the Population Density of the House Sparrow Passer domesticus niloticus L. and Their Relationship of Damage on Wheat Crop (Triticum aestivum L.)
abstractText: Habitat type and environmental diversity around agroecosystems are key ecological factors influencing organism distribution and reproduction. Habitat diversity, ranging from tree cover and built structures to waterways, plays a crucial role in reshaping pest population dynamics by providing safe refuges, nesting sites, and food sources. These environmental changes directly impact pest population densities, resulting in varying levels of loss and damage to strategic economic crops. Passer domesticu s niloticus, commonly known as the house sparrow, poses a significant threat to crops and causes substantial damage in agriculture and horticulture. It particularly thrives in regions of Egypt where it can reproduce rapidly, leading to substantial population increases and consequent damage. This study aimed to assess the effect of habitat type on the population density of the house sparrow Passer ‎domesticus niloticus L. and its relationship of damage on wheat Triticum aestivum L. Three different habitats ‎ were used: Building, tree, and Canal water. The results indicated that the wheat nearby of trees habitat was the most population. Followed by Building and Canal water habitats. Also, the results demonstrated a strong, direct correlation between the availability of arboreal habitats and increased population density of the Nile house sparrow P. domesticus niloticus a trend that negatively impacted productivity rates and led to greater direct crop losses in wheat T. aestivum ‎ fields. On the other hand, the study revealed that the milky stage of grain development is the most vulnerable to damage compared to the initial formation or dry maturity stages.

title: From practice to policy: Bridging the research-practice gap in African nursing
abstractText: Trends in Nursing (TIN) publishes contemporary and relevant research and evidence-based information on the nursing profession. The aim is to make information accessible to scholars, educators, clinical practitioners, nurse managers, and policy makers to advance planning and decision-making in nursing education, research, quality improvement initiatives, nursing regulation, and workforce planning. The articles should provide a description of current developments in nursing in Africa or an overview of global developments in nursing.

title: Students’ everyday sexism in language: A case study at a South African university
abstractText: Gender-based violence remains a pervasive crisis in South Africa, with everyday sexist language undermining campus inclusivity. This article investigates the manifestation, nature and influence of sexist language at a university in Pretoria, exploring how intersectional and cultural factors exacerbate gendered exclusion. A convergent mixed-methods approach was employed, gathering data from 110 student questionnaires and three face-to-face focus-group interviews (10 students per group). Findings confirm that sexist language perpetuates entrenched biases that marginalise women, men and lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, intersex, asexual (LGBTQIA+) students alike. To foster an equitable academic environment, the researchers recommend policy reforms, institutional sensitisation training and proactive awareness campaigns. Ultimately, this study advances scholarship on language, social justice and higher-education reform. Contribution: By examining the experiences of students across different gender identities and sexual orientations, this article addresses a critical research gap in peer-to-peer campus discourse. It provides empirical and theoretical insights into the normalisation of everyday linguistic sexism, demonstrating how communicative practices shape gender bias, social norms and institutional inclusivity in higher education.

title: Quality and completeness of magnetic resonance enterography reporting in Crohn’s disease
abstractText: Background: Magnetic resonance enterography (MRE) is central to evaluating Crohn’s disease (CD), allowing multiplanar assessment of inflammatory activity, luminal narrowing, penetrating disease and extraintestinal involvement, without exposure to ionising radiation. The 2022 European Crohn’s and Colitis Organization (ECCO) and European Society of Gastrointestinal and Abdominal Radiology (ESGAR) topical review emphasises standardised reporting to improve clinical utility. This study audited MRE reporting quality for CD at a tertiary public sector healthcare facility in South Africa against international reporting guidelines by assessing documentation of predefined technical and radiological reporting elements, use of standardised terminology, and the relationship between report structure and readability. Methods: A retrospective descriptive audit of 100 consecutive adult MRE studies performed between December 2021 and August 2023 was conducted. Reports were reviewed for inclusion of technical and radiological features, use of accepted nomenclature and report structure. Frequencies were expressed as percentages, and categorical associations were tested using Chi-square or Fisher’s exact methods. Results: Technical parameters were seldom documented (8%). Disease activity was present in 69%, absent in 28% and omitted in 3%. Complications were noted in 44%, predominantly strictures and fistulae. Structured formats were used in half the reports and were significantly associated with improved readability (p < 0.001), though not with overall comprehensiveness. Only 38% of conclusions used standardised nomenclature, and no reporting domain achieved the arbitrary 70% adequacy benchmark. Conclusion: Magnetic resonance enterography reporting for CD at the research facility demonstrated variable completeness and inconsistent terminology. Contribution: Adoption of structured templates aligned with ECCO–ESGAR guidance may improve clarity, consistency and clinical value. Targeted education and multidisciplinary feedback are recommended to enhance reporting standards and support patient care.

Diagnostics of the sustainable development of industrial enterprises in the monitoring system of the regional economy
abstractText: Subject. Diagnostics of the sustainable development of industrial enterprises as the primary level of monitoring of the regional economy. Objectives. To propose and test a two-block methodology for diagnosing the sustainable development of industrial enterprises, to substantiate its calculated parameters – the weights of indicators, threshold criteria for scoring and the scale of interpretation of the integral index, to determine the possibilities of applying aggregated results in regional industrial monitoring. Methods. The research is based on system, process, resource, and risk-based approaches. The assessment was based on fixed documentary criteria, normalization, calculation of partial and integral indices, and sensitivity analysis. Equal weights of indicators and blocks are accepted in accordance with the principle of insufficient foundation. Results. A methodology is proposed that combines eight organizational and eight economic indicators, partial, integral and aggregated indexes, and eight analytical contours. The zone of permissible deviation ±5% when converting indicators into points and a five-level equal-interval scale of interpretation of the integral index are substantiated. The methodology is applicable to assess the sustainable development of enterprises, their cross–industry comparison and identification of risk areas, and the diagnostic results are used to justify management decisions and targeted measures of regional industrial policy. Conclusions. A joint review of organizational and economic indicators makes it possible to determine which factors contribute to the sustainability of each enterprise. Even with similar values of the integral index, enterprises differ in the composition and severity of the identified limitations. The aggregated index characterizes only the surveyed population and is not an assessment of the entire industrial complex of the region.

title: Understanding teachers' curriculum reform receptivity: a psychological and cognitive perspective
abstractText: Purpose This study examined teachers' curriculum receptivity by integrating pedagogical beliefs, perceived benefits and costs, cognitive load and reform fatigue within a unified psychological framework. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey of 784 in-service teachers in the Teacher Professional Education (PPG) program was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping to assess measurement validity and structural relationships. Findings Attitude was the strongest predictor of curriculum receptivity. Germane load had the largest positive effect on attitude and contributed to receptivity both directly and indirectly. Perceived benefits positively affect both attitude and receptivity, whereas reform fatigue has a negative effect. Intrinsic load had a small but significant positive effect on attitude and an indirect effect on receptivity, although its direct effect on receptivity was not significant. Pedagogical beliefs, perceived costs and extraneous load showed limited or non-significant effects. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation, and the sample's concentration in Sulawesi may affect generalisability. This study contributes theoretically by treating curriculum receptivity as a psychologically mediated outcome and distinguishing the roles of different types of cognitive load. Practical implications Curriculum reform should promote meaningful teacher engagement through active learning, communicate benefits clearly and manage reform fatigue, rather than relying solely on reducing workload or changing beliefs. Originality/value This study offers an integrated model that highlights the central roles of attitude and productive cognitive engagement in shaping teachers' acceptance of curriculum reforms.

Artificial Intelligence in Legal Proceedings: Constitutional Limits
abstractText: Based on the Concept for the Introduction of AI Technologies in Judicial Proceedings of the Russian Federation (2026), the authors examine the transition from electronic justice to the digital intellectualization of judicial activity. The central issue is the permissible degree of algorithmic influence and the constitutional-legal limits of using artificial intelligence in judicial proceedings. A risk-oriented model of legal regulation is proposed, based on the differentiation of AI functions by the degree of their impact on constitutional rights and principles of judicial proceedings, while preserving the exclusive role of the judge. Drawing on an analysis of the practice of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation and doctrinal sources, the necessity of special guarantees for high-risk functions is substantiated. A constitutional standard for the admissibility of judicial AI is formulated. Directions for improving procedural legislation are proposed.

title: Groundwater in the regions of Russia
abstractText: Subject. Control over valuable strategic resources. Objectives. Outline the current problems and factors for the effective use of groundwater, taking into account the development of the global market for non-bottled water. Methods. Statistical, comparative analyses. Results. A comparative assessment of the distribution of groundwater deposits across the federal districts has been carried out, trends in the dynamics of groundwater extraction and their pollution levels have been identified. Promising innovative solutions and possibilities of neural network technologies for protecting the water conservation system have been considered. Conclusions. Amid negative climate changes, groundwater is becoming a reliable source of water supply.

title: The development of internal audit in the context of crop production digitalization
abstractText: Subject. This article looks at a mix of theoretical, methodological, and practical questions about organizing internal audits of the use of drones in crop farming in the context of the digitalization of the agro-industrial complex. Objectives. The article aims to develop theoretical principles and practical recommendations for organizing internal audits of agro-drones usage in crop production, an audit methodology that includes checking the validity of routes and application rates, monitoring the completeness and quality of work, evaluating resource use efficiency, as well as creating an algorithm for integrating telemetry data into the accounting system for automated material write-offs. Methods. For the study, we used analysis and synthesis, a systems approach, classification, comparison, generalization, as well as risk management methods and modeling of control procedures. Results. The article presents an author-developed three-level methodology for internal auditing of agro-drone usage and proposes an algorithm for integrating telemetry data into the accounting system, consisting of seven consecutive steps – from creating a digital flight mission to monitoring deviations by the internal audit service. The article also presents an author-developed form of an electronic primary document, the Log of Agro-Drone Performed Operations, which ensures the transformation of technical information into an accounting document. Conclusions and Relevance. The proposed method and algorithm create a closed-loop system for managing the use of agro-drones – from planning flight missions to material write-offs and evaluating effectiveness. The approach ensures accurate accounting by automatically generating primary documents based on verified telemetry data, preventing unwarranted resource write-offs. This turns internal auditing into a tool for managing the risks of digitalizing crop production. The results obtained can be used by internal audit services and management of agricultural organizations of various sizes to improve control and risk management systems when implementing drone technologies, and they can also be applied in the educational process when training specialists in economic security, auditing, and accounting in the agricultural sector.

title: On the issue of defining the concept of Catching-up Old Industrial Regions
abstractText: Subject. Diversifying the economy of industrial regions. Objectives. Based on the theory of institutional path dependence, identify and justify the constitutive features of catching-up old industrial regions. Methods. General scientific research methods were applied. Results. The phenomenon of the 'Ural trap' most fully reflects the specifics of the development of old industrial regions, representing a deep institutional dependence on the past trajectory of development. Conclusions. The research results can be used when developing a new type of targeted economic policy.

title: Process indexes of digital transformation of domestic companies: Main development trends
abstractText: Subject. Process-based digital transformation indices of Russian public companies, calculated on the basis of text analysis of annual reports using the B. Kindermann dictionary. Objectives. To identify the main trends in the development of digital transformation across the following dimensions: digital architecture configuration, digital capabilities, digital ecosystem coordination, and the scope of digital technologies. Methods. The empirical base includes financial data and annual reports of 153 Russian public companies for 2014–2024. Component-specific and aggregate digital transformation indices are constructed, along with industry rankings based on the process-based digital orientation index. Correlation analysis is applied. Results. The aggregate process-based digital orientation index of Russian public companies shows sustained growth. The increase is unevenly distributed across its components. The dynamics of the aggregate index across the leading industries confirm the sustained leadership of the telecommunications sector throughout the observation period, while the indicator in the information technology, retail, and construction sectors exhibits strong year-to-year volatility. Conclusions. The results confirm the gap between declared digital orientation and the actual level of technology adoption known from the literature. This may indicate the specifics of the Russian digitalization model, which is oriented toward internal infrastructure rather than ecosystem interactions. Without changes to the organizational model and business strategy, digital tools deliver only a limited effect.

title: Penerapan Fungsi Manajemen pada Usaha Jual Beli Kayu CV. Mitra Abadi Kota Palu
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dan menganalisis penerapan fungsi manajemen POAC (planning, organizing, actuating, dan controlling) dalam pengelolaan usaha jual beli kayu pada CV. Mitra Abadi Kota Palu. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan teknik pengumpulan data melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi. Teori yang digunakan adalah teori fungsi manajemen George R. Terry. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa keempat fungsi manajemen telah diterapkan secara sederhana dan fungsional sesuai dengan skala usaha. Pada aspek perencanaan, usaha dikembangkan secara bertahap dari modal yang sederhana, dengan pasokan kayu dari berbagai daerah dan harga yang mengikuti harga pasar. Pada aspek pengorganisasian, struktur organisasi bersifat ramping dengan pembagian tugas yang jelas antara pimpinan dan dua tenaga lapangan. Pada aspek pelaksanaan, penggerakan tenaga kerja dilakukan melalui arahan langsung dan komunikasi yang bersifat kekeluargaan. Pada aspek pengawasan, penyortiran kayu dilakukan setiap ada bongkaran masuk dan evaluasi hasil usaha dilakukan setiap bulan. Meskipun demikian, pencatatan keuangan dan stok secara tertulis masih perlu diperkuat. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa fungsi manajemen POAC pada CV. Mitra Abadi telah berjalan secara praktis di lapangan, namun diperlukan penguatan pencatatan, perencanaan cadangan pasokan, dan penjadwalan yang lebih terukur.

title: Using stochastic modeling within the foresight technology when developing regional strategic development plans
abstractText: Subject. Development of forecasting and planning methods that take into account a high level of uncertainty. Objectives. Justifying the need to move from deterministic forecasting to probabilistic scenario methods. Developing and testing a methodology for allocating budget funds that minimizes the risk of not achieving target indicators when dealing with unfavorable scenarios. Methods. Simulation modeling, scenario analysis, stochastic optimization. Results. Using a hypothetical region as an example, it shows that evenly distributing budget funds ultimately gives the highest average effect but has low resilience in a crisis scenario. The maximin strategy, focused on the worst-case scenario, increases the level of guaranteed results but lowers the average effect. The foresight-stochastic strategy helps balance efficiency and risk. Conclusions. The proposed methodology can be used by regional authorities and strategic planning centers as a tool to choose how to allocate resources in situations of high external uncertainty.

title: AR-based culture therapy in the heritage tourism site: from two different perspectives of mindfulness
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to resolve the conceptual fragmentation in technology-mediated well-being research by investigating augmented reality’s (AR) role as a digital cotherapist at the Liangzhu archaeological ruins. It seeks to unpack the mechanisms through which AR cultivates dual mindfulness pathways – meditative and sociocognitive, and to differentiate their heterogeneous effects on visitor well-being. Furthermore, it clarifies the triadic synergy between the heritage environment, AR affordances and user characteristics, challenging simplistic attributions of therapeutic outcomes to technology alone. Ultimately, the study proposes a dynamic typology of mindfulness experiences to guide the design of AR-enhanced cultural therapy interventions. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on twenty-one semistructured interviews with individuals who used AR glasses at a museum located in a World Heritage Site – the archaeological ruins of Liangzhu City – this research systematically examines the antecedents, processes and consequences of mindfulness. Findings By screening users who have genuinely engaged in meditative mindfulness with three criteria attention, present moment and nonjudgment, as well as sociocognitive mindfulness using three criteria – novelty seeking, novelty producing and engagement, this study develops a novel framework for understanding mindfulness in heritage tourism. Originality/value This study introduces a sensory-cognitive continuum, which challenges a binary conceptualization of mindfulness types. It reveals a dynamic interplay between meditative and sociocognitive states within single AR experiences. This study develops a preliminary typology of AR-mediated mindfulness experiences, distinguishing four configurations: (1) predominantly meditative; (2) predominantly sociocognitive; (3) cooccurring (both types simultaneously); and (4) sequential (movement between types).

title: The role of Harry and Fred Struben in the discovery of the gold deposits of the Witwatersrand region
abstractText: The Struben family emigrated from Europe to Durban in 1850 and relocated to Pretoria in 1885. Two of their sons, Harry and Fred, would become involved in mineral exploration. Harry participated in the early Kimberley diamond rush and later exploited gold at Lydenburg (Pilgrim’s Rest) and Barberton. The Strubens formed a prospecting partnership, with Harry doing the administration while Fred undertook fieldwork. They purchased portions of three farms near present-day Roodepoort (Sterkfontein, Zwartkop and Wilgespruit) where limited mining was taking place and began systematic prospecting in January 1884. In September 1884, they discovered the Confidence Reef, a rich but small quartz vein on Wilgespruit. Fred drew an outcrop map of this prospect area, plotting quartz veins and geographical features that make it possible for us to georeference this map. A comparison of his georeferenced map with the map of Mellor (Geol Surv South Africa Spec Pub 197. 1917;3:46), revealed that Fred Struben’s map included the basal portion of the Witwatersrand sequence, but excluded the Jeppestown Subgroup and the overlying Main Reef Group. For 2 years (1884–1885), Fred Struben searched for gold-bearing quartz veins and only became aware of the gold-bearing Main Reef conglomerate in May 1886. The Strubens obtained an interest in a small portion of Main Reef on the farm Langlaagte and more extensive interests on the far fringes of the Main Reef outcrop zone. In late 1886–1887, the mining industry transformed its financial structures. At this critical time (February 1887), Harry Struben emigrated from the Transvaal Republic, settling in Cape Town, while Fred Struben retired to a manor house in Devonshire in the UK.

title: Overtime modalities and turnover intention: associations with work–leisure imbalance, domain-attributed pressure and job satisfaction
abstractText: Purpose This study examines how extended-hours work, after-hours electronic assignments and combined exposure are associated with work–leisure imbalance (WLI), domain-attributed pressure, job satisfaction and turnover intention. Design/methodology/approach Survey-weighted models with reconstructed design variables analyzed 4,095 Taiwanese national wage workers covered by labor insurance. Multinomial logit models assessed modality membership. An observed-variable generalized structural equation model linked the outcomes. Recursive g-computation decomposed turnover-probability differences using 5,000 primary bootstrap replicates and bias-corrected and accelerated intervals. Four sensitivity analyses used 5,000 replicates each under a common collapsed-strata bootstrap with percentile intervals. Findings All overtime modalities were associated with higher WLI. Primary full serial associations with turnover intention were 0.082–0.237 percentage points, below 2.2% of the respective totals. Serial associations remained positive in all four sensitivity analyzes but increased substantially with age-and-sex-only adjustment. Extended-hours-only total intervals included zero under full-time restriction and the alternative exposure definition. Total and serial contrasts are exploratory and unadjusted for multiplicity; they do not confirm a stronger mechanism for combined exposure. Combined and electronic-only total associations were not statistically distinguishable. Originality/value Distinguishing exposure modalities and separating total from serial associations clarify the small primary serial components and their sensitivity to adjustment, without identifying causal mediation or a distinct combined-exposure mechanism.

title: Development of weak signal methodology: Phase diagnostics of changes in management systems
abstractText: Subject. Early diagnostics of structural changes in financial, economic, and managerial systems based on weak signal analysis. Objectives. To develop a phase-based approach to assessing the sustainability of organizations, enabling the identification of pre-crisis states before they manifest in financial and market indicators. Methods. A synthesis of methods of systems and morphological analysis, the provisions of nonlinear dynamics, and the concept of weak signals is used. Results. It is shown that financial sustainability is determined by the configuration of internal and external ties, whereas traditional indicators reflect delayed effects of structural changes. It is substantiated that weak signals capture early shifts in the architecture of interactions and precede the deterioration of financial metrics. A phase model is proposed that interprets the development of a system as a sequence of stable configurations, and the Fibonacci sequence as an analytical scale of structural thresholds and saturation levels. It is shown that structural dynamics can develop while the statistical stability of indicators is preserved. Conclusions and Relevance. The phase-based approach enables a shift from the ex post detection of deviations to the identification of structural preconditions for crisis, reduces the lag of managerial responses, and lays the foundation for anticipatory management. The results are applicable to tasks of financial sustainability diagnostics, risk management, analysis of corporate dynamics, and the development of decision support systems.

Comparison of econometric approaches and machine learning methods for nowcasting of income and expenses of the consolidated budget of the Russian Federation
abstractText: Subject. Nowcasting of revenues and expenditures of the consolidated budget of the Russian Federation based on econometric and neural network models. Objectives. Comparison of the predictive quality of a wide range of machine learning models and classical autoregression with exogenous variables when forecasting total income, individual income items and budget expenditures for one month in advance. Methods. Based on the monthly consolidated budget execution data for January 2012 – May 2025, the forward propagation neural network (FFNN), recurrent network (LSTM), convolutional network (CNN), Transformer architecture, gradient boosting over decision trees (CatBoost), as well as the ARX model and naive prediction as benchmarks were considered. All rows have been converted to growth rates for the corresponding month of the previous year without seasonal adjustment; the number of epochs and trees, as well as the number of ARX lags, are selected from the validation sample; The quality of the forecast is measured by the root of the root mean square error (RMSE) in the test sample (June 2023 – May 2025). Results. Based on the monthly consolidated budget execution data for January 2012 – May 2025, the forward propagation neural network (FFNN), recurrent network (LSTM), convolutional network (CNN), Transformer architecture, gradient boosting over decision trees (CatBoost), as well as the ARX model and naive prediction as benchmarks were considered. All rows have been converted to growth rates for the corresponding month of the previous year without seasonal adjustment; the number of epochs and trees, as well as the number of ARX lags, are selected from the validation sample; The quality of the forecast is measured by the root of the root mean square error (RMSE) in the test sample (June 2023 – May 2025). For 6 out of 11 indicators, machine learning models outperformed the ARX model and the naive forecast in accuracy; FFNN and CNN architectures provided the best quality forecasts of total and non-oil and gas revenues. For oil and gas revenues and expenses, the simpler ARX model, based on oil prices and the real exchange rate, retained the advantage, which indicates the predominantly linear nature of the dependence of these items on market conditions. The Diebold – Mariano test confirms the superiority of machine learning at a 5% level only in terms of insurance premiums for compulsory social insurance; for the rest, the observed gain of 18-32% does not reach significance, which is mainly due to the low test power on a test sample of 24 observations and does not mean equal accuracy of the models. Conclusions. Neural network models are a promising tool for tracking budget indicators even on relatively short rows and with minimal hyperparameter tuning, and their potential can be further unlocked by fine-tuning architectures. Since a short sample does not allow us to statistically confirm most of the observed differences, it is preferable to combine forecasts rather than choosing a single model.; The use of neural network models in the budget process is limited by short series, weak interpretability and incorrect extrapolation in scenario calculations.

Neither truck nor train, rather truck on train: innovative freight fusion or patchwork?
abstractText: Learning outcomes After completion of the case study, the students will be able to Case overview/synopsis Banas Dairy was Asia’s largest dairy cooperative. It transported liquid milk from its Palanpur plant, Gujarat to Faridabad plant, Delhi National Capital Region. For this transportation, Banas dairy used railway milk tankers (RMTs) and road transport. These modes inherently had some concerns. For example, in RMTs there were frequent delays, repetitive milk transfers and increased costs due to demurrage charged by Indian Railways (IR). Along with that, another grave issue was maintaining the quality of milk. In trucking mode, truck drivers had to undergo risks of pilferage, road accidents and police harassment. In 2021, the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) offered the ToT service on its Western Dedicated Corridor of India (The Economic Times, 2025a). Part A of this case was positioned around six months before the Banas Dairy actually adopted the ToT. That time, conundrum was whether Banas Dairy would change its transportation mode to the ToT. The conundrum faced by Banas Dairy would have to be resolved under the able guidance of Mr Sangram R. Chaudhary, managing director of Banas Dairy. The change was to be implemented in the immediate future to overcome the cons posed by the RMTs and road transport. Part B of this case, which was based on 2023–2026 and covered the period after the shift to ToT mode, showed another dilemma – how to optimize the return journey of the ToT. This case study detailed the operations of the DFCCIL and the salient features of the ToT. It highlighted logistics improvements, savings in fuel costs and the positive environmental effects of innovative logistics, especially in rail transport, in a developing economy such as India. This is a teaching note supplementing the “Neither truck nor train, rather truck on train: innovative freight fusion or patchwork?” case study. Complexity academic level This case study is designed for undergraduate or graduate-level programs in supply chain and logistics or strategy management, and senior management professionals in executive education programs undertaking courses in logistics management, supply chain operations and related cargo logistics. Subject code CSS 9: Operations and Logistics.

title: Modeling of consensus protocols of the digital ruble trust infrastructure
abstractText: Subject. This article discusses the assessment of the Raft consensus protocol stability in the context of the digital ruble trust infrastructure. Objectives. The study aims to develop a computer model that allows analyzing the behavior of a distributed cluster in the event of network delays, message losses, node failures, and attacks. Methods. For the study, we used the methods of discrete event modeling. Results. The article conducts a series of computational experiments, during which estimates the proportion of time with a single leader, the average number of simultaneously active leaders, message delivery, the number of malicious messages, and system recovery time. Conclusions. The paper creates a discrete-event model of the Raft consensus protocol, designed to study the behavior of a distributed cluster during network delays, node failures, and attacks.

title: Spatial optimization of asset placement in a polycentric urban agglomeration within a regional socioeconomic complex
abstractText: Subject. Factors, constraints, criteria, and calculation procedures that determine the spatial optimization of the placement of production and infrastructure assets in a polycentric urban agglomeration. Objectives. Development of a formalized model for spatial optimization of placing production and infrastructure assets in a polycentric urban agglomeration. Methods. The study is based on a two-level decision-making logic, which includes a preliminary selection of territorial alternatives and a subsequent overall assessment of the acceptable placement options across a set of criteria. Results. A two-level model of spatial optimization has been proposed. It has been found that using a polycentric criterion of spatial inclusion allows for a more accurate consideration of the role of secondary subcenters in the urban agglomeration and improves the precision of the final ranking of asset placement options. The proposed integrated assessment of territorial alternatives makes it possible to move towards a quantitatively justified decision that takes into account the strategic goals of developing the regional socio-economic complex. Conclusions. The application of the developed model creates conditions for improving the efficiency of public and private investments, reducing the risk of making uncoordinated decisions in spatial development, and forming a more sustainable polycentric structure of the urban agglomeration.

title: Empirical analysis of competitiveness of sea port operators in the Azov-Black Sea basin
abstractText: Subject. Competitiveness of the sea port operators of the Azov-Black Sea basin in the context of digital transformation, assessed according to open sources. Objectives. Empirical testing of the author's methodology for integrated quantitative assessment of the competitiveness of port operators using the example of PJSC NCSP and JSC TMTP for 2021–2024, identification of the dynamics of their competitive positions and determination of growth reserves. Methods. The research is based on the methods of systematic and comparative analysis. The calculations were performed using minimax normalization of indicators, additive aggregation of group indexes into an integral indicator, and analysis of the sensitivity of the model to variations in weighting coefficients. Results. A practical test of the three-block methodology was carried out using data from two key port operators in the region. The group indexes of the production, financial, digital blocks and the intensity of use of the port infrastructure, as well as the consolidated integral index of competitiveness are calculated. It has been established that NCSP PJSC is steadily increasing its competitive advantages, while TMTP JSC remains in a zone of low competitiveness. Conclusions. Empirical testing has confirmed the operability and practical significance of the proposed toolkit. The methodology allows you to rank operators, identify the sources of their competitive advantages and problem areas. The toolkit can be used by port operators for self–diagnosis, regulators for monitoring digitalization processes, and the scientific community for benchmarking port operators.

title: Applicability of Russia's energy strategy for the structural modernization of domestic oil refining
abstractText: Subject. This article focuses on the problems of regulatory and legal support for the policy of ensuring the deep modernization of the Russian oil refining. Objectives. The study aims to assess the applicability of Russia's Energy Strategy for the implementation of deep modernization of domestic oil refining. Methods. For the study, I used methods of comparative analysis and generalization of information from State authorities of the Russian Federation. Results. The article reveals that Russia has sufficient potential to tap into reserves of production capacities, with the exception of conditions for the implementation of a stress scenario. It also determines that it is advisable to use the indicator of the light petroleum products yield, while the depth of oil refining is more appropriate as an auxiliary value. Conclusions. The Energy Strategy does not seem to be a significant document from the perspective of ensuring the structural modernization of oil refining yet. It is necessary to review not only the refining indicators of the Energy Strategy, but also the structure of the document itself.

title: Technological vulnerabilities of decentralized finance: Implications for the security of national payment systems
abstractText: Subject. The essence of blockchain technology and its impact on the security of decentralized financial services. Objectives. To identify the technological and regulatory limitations of the blockchain in its potential application in national payment systems. Analysis of the Bitcoin architecture. Methods. The study is based on the deconstruction of the technical principles of the blockchain, an expert assessment of vulnerability cases, a comparison of fraud statistics in traditional payment systems and cryptocurrency services, as well as a study of central banks' initiatives to introduce DLT technologies. Results. It has been revealed that the blockchain provides cryptographic protection of transactions, but does not eliminate the risks of social engineering and malicious software. At the same time, bitcoin mining consumes resources comparable to the energy consumption of entire countries, which creates environmental and economic constraints. It is noted that the lack of centralized responsibility (for example, the loss of private keys and wallet hacking) shifts all risks onto users, reducing trust in them from both the private and corporate sectors, as well as government agencies. At the same time, large payment operators integrate crypto tools, maintaining centralized control through identity verification systems and geographical restrictions, forming hybrid centralized-decentralized models. Conclusions. The security of decentralized finance is determined not by the technological perfection of the blockchain, but by the presence of a clear regulatory framework, the responsibility of operators and the protection of user rights. The scalability trilemma (the inability to simultaneously achieve high security, decentralization, and processing speed) remains a fundamental limitation for the use of blockchain in national payment systems. The prospects for introducing DeFi technologies into national payment systems are related to the development of international regulatory standards, quantum-stable algorithms, and clear standards of platform responsibility.

title: Business analytics of information resources and information technology management
abstractText: Subject. Business analytics of data management, information resources, technologies and knowledge. Objectives. To propose options for effective methodological approaches, methods and tools for business analysis of data, information resources and information technologies used for their management and optimization based on modern information systems and business intelligence. Methods. Empirical methods (direct observation, conducting surveys, questionnaires and interviews), analytical, descriptive methods, etc. were used. Results. Legislative and regulatory acts, methodologies, standards, and tools for managing data, information resources, and technologies and knowledge aimed at ensuring effective, secure management of IT assets are analyzed. Conclusions. IT enterprises can improve their customer service by using a range of IT technologies and CRM system applications to create large amounts of customer data, manage databases, primarily information resources and knowledge. This guarantees extensive customer feedback and allows you to analyze and interpret, predict and constructively use the obtained business intelligence to make managerial decisions.

title: Detection of the invasive land snail Caucasotachea vindobonensis (helicidae) in the Mordovia State Nature Reserve (European Russia)
abstractText: A non-native terrestrial gastropod, Caucasotachea vindobonensis, was recorded for the first time in the Mordovia State Nature Reserve (Pushta settlement, Temnikovsky District, Republic of Mordovia, European Russia). A single specimen was found near the Reserve's visitor center; its shell dimensions and morphology correspond to those typical of the species. The record expands knowledge of the species' distribution in the central part of the Russian Plain. The most likely pathway of introduction is accidental transport by motor vehicles, although intentional transport by visitors is also possible. Because the specimen may already be fertilized, establishment of a viable population within the protected ecosystem is possible. A single record does not indicate an invasion, since a non-native species becomes invasive only at high abundance and with a negative impact on native ecosystem components; eradication is therefore not necessarily required, but regular monitoring of the Reserve is needed to detect potential spread at an early stage and to assess its impact on local biocenoses.

title: Comprehensive system and mechanism of State regulation of scientific and technological development of the Donetsk People's Republic
abstractText: Subject. Formation of a comprehensive system of State regulation in the scientific and technological sphere of the Donetsk People's Republic. Objectives. To determine the content of the integrated system and mechanism of State regulation of scientific and technological development of the Donetsk People's Republic. Methods. The validity, reliability and argumentation of the research results are ensured by the use of systems analysis, formal logic, general scientific methods of cognition: analysis and synthesis, induction and deduction, generalization. Results. The possible components of an integrated system of scientific and technological development, which in one form or another can be implemented in the region, are highlighted and presented in the form of rulers. The components that are currently not being implemented in the DPR have been identified. For the purposes of State regulation of scientific and technological development, systematic and functional approaches to the formation of a mechanism of state regulation are proposed. The implementation of a systems approach based on the analysis of the powers and identified relationships of public authorities has allowed us to propose a model of an integrated system that reveals the content of the mechanism of State regulation and the most comprehensive system of State regulation of scientific and technological development of the Republic. Conclusions. The selected lines of components, representing the composition of possible components of an integrated system of State regulation of scientific and technological development, are of practical importance and can be used by the subjects of the Russian Federation to build an integrated system in their regions.

title: Standardization of audit activities: Theory and practice of application
abstractText: Subject. This article discusses the issues related to the standardization of auditing activities, which helps make the process of providing audit services more transparent, streamline management processes, and improve the quality of services provided. Objectives. The article aims to analyze the main systems of auditing standardization and focus on certain aspects of organizing an audit at the stages of planning, carrying out audit procedures, collecting and evaluating evidence, as well as documenting, considering a specific business entity as a case study. This will help prove the need to use audit standards to unify the process of carrying out an audit engagement. Methods. For the study, we used analysis and synthesis, as well as graphical methods. Results. The article finds that standardizing auditing activities makes the process of completing audit engagements more uniform, helps save labor and financial resources, streamlines the inspection process, and improves the quality of the services provided. Conclusions and Relevance. The examined process of auditing standardization shows a merging of two different directions, namely international legislative literature and national regulatory systems, which helps ensure the unification of activities, resource savings, and quality of auditing services at a new level. The results presented can be used in the theory and practice of auditing firms that have entered into an audit contract.

title: The University amidst ‘Knowledge Abundance’: Reconsidering the Values of Higher Education in the Age of Generative AI
An Immoral Offence by an Educator: The Concept and Classification
abstractText: The article analyzes the concept of “immoral misconduct” from the point of view of labor law theory and the position of the courts. The problems of qualification of immoral misconduct in various situations are outlined. The author’s interpretation of this definition is proposed. It is concluded that it is advisable to establish commissions in each subject of the Russian Federation to protect the professional honor and dignity of teaching staff upon termination of an employment contract under clause 8, Part 1, Article 81 of the Labor Code of the Russian Federation, and to introduce mandatory consideration of their opinions. The recommendations will improve the current labor legislation and protect the rights of teaching staff.

title: The concept of financial models for scaling artificial intelligence systems for development and security
abstractText: Subject. The concept of financial models for scaling artificial intelligence (AI) systems in the context of development and security. Objectives. Suggest and justify new financial models for scaling AI systems that provide companies and organizations with safe development and effective investment in AI technologies. Methods. An interdisciplinary approach is applied, combining elements of risk management theory, AI economics, and security studies. Results. The challenges and risks associated with the process of scaling AI systems are detailed. The Comprehensive System for Secure Scaling of AI Systems is proposed and argued. The specific features of financial planning for the secure scaling of AI systems are substantiated. Based on existing financial mechanisms, alternative models of this process are proposed. Methods for evaluating the efficiency of investments in this process are identified and grouped by functional criterion. Conclusions and Relevance. The concept of financial models for the secure scaling of AI systems, as a comprehensive and multi-level approach, is essential for expanding the practical capabilities of AI and guaranteeing its security, ethics, and sustainability. The proposed security system encompasses risk management, continuous monitoring, and adaptation of advanced technologies. Evaluating the efficiency of investments in the secure scaling of AI systems goes beyond traditional financial metrics and therefore requires consideration of quantitative and qualitative aspects, economic benefits, innovation potential, competitiveness, pricing, and ethical factors. The results can be applied in managing resources and capital when scaling AI platforms, assessing related financial risks, ensuring security, as well as in developing regulatory frameworks and attracting investments.

title: Digital transformation of preferential treatment management in order to increase their effectiveness and spatial development of the country
abstractText: Subject. This article focuses on the digital transformation of preferential treatment management in order to increase their effectiveness, eliminate systemic problems and achieve the goals of the country's spatial development in the context of the uberization processes spread. Objectives. The study aims to develop the concept of a unified digital ecosystem of preferential regimes. Methods. For the study, I used the methods of logical, structural and institutional analyses. Results. The article highlights three levels of preferential treatment management problems in Russia, and substantiates the necessity of digital transformation of preferential treatment management. It also identifies and describes the key components of the preferential treatment management unified digital ecosystem. Conclusions. The digital transformation of preferential treatment management is changing the logic of interaction between authorities and residents. Management is moving from administration to creating an environment for development and reducing spatial differentiation. The results of the study can help the developers of preferential and State regional policies, strategic planning authorities and management companies of preferential regimes.

title: Decolonising science through a convivial lens: Moving from academic enclosure to shared incompleteness. Comments on Ndlovu-Gatsheni (2026)
Features of the economic safety diagnostics state of nuclear industry construction organizations
abstractText: Subject. This article discusses the organizational and methodological approaches for diagnosing the economic safety state of nuclear industry construction organizations. Objectives. The study aims to develop methodological approaches for diagnosing the state of economic security, taking into account industry specifics in the field of nuclear power plant construction. Methods. For the study, I used the methods of systems approach, theoretical analysis and classification, as well as structural analysis. Results. The article reveals the limitations of traditional approaches for diagnosing the economic safety of the nuclear industry, and outlines five key features that determine the specifics of the nuclear power plants construction. It also develops an author's system of indicators to offset the existing limitations in traditional approaches, proposes calculation formulas and thresholds. Conclusions. The proposed author's indicators make it possible to take into account industry-specific features and improve the efficiency of diagnosing the state of economic security. The research results can be helpful for the economic safety departments of construction organizations in the nuclear industry.

title: Development of the theoretical foundations for forming and strengthening the innovative potential of aerospace industry enterprises
abstractText: Subject. The innovation potential of cooperating companies in the aerospace industry within a unified value chain. Objectives. To advance the theoretical foundations of building and strengthening the innovation potential of aerospace industry enterprises. Methods. The study employs a set of theoretical analysis methods, a systems approach, comparative analysis, scientific generalization, and structuring. Results. The economic content of the concept of "innovation potential of industry enterprises" is refined, defined as the totality of resources, competencies, technological capabilities, and institutional conditions for innovation activities distributed among cooperation participants. The key factors of its development are systematized and grouped by technological, cooperative, resource, organizational-managerial, institutional, and reproductive aspects. Conclusions and Relevance. Practical recommendations are formulated, aimed at strengthening coordination in value chains, creating an integrated knowledge management system, applying agile project management methods, and purposefully fostering a favorable institutional environment for doing business. Development of methodological tools for the quantitative assessment of the innovation potential of enterprises; study of knowledge management and intellectual property mechanisms within industry alliances; examination of the impact of digitalization and the adoption of end-to-end technologies on the evolution of forms of cooperation.

title: Digital readiness as an enabling capability for HyFlex-VR learning in vocational education
abstractText: Purpose This study examines how perceived HyFlex-VR affordances and digital readiness relate to vocational students' learning experiences and whether readiness operates as a direct enabling capability or moderates the affordance–experience relationship. Design/methodology/approach A quantitatively dominant embedded mixed-method study involved 187 vocational high school students from South Sulawesi, Indonesia. After response quality screening, 169 cases were analysed using disjoint two-stage partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Digital readiness (digital infrastructure and competence) and learning experience (engagement and satisfaction) were modelled as formative higher-order composites. Open-ended survey responses were used to supplement the quantitative analysis. Findings Perceived HyFlex-VR affordances (ß = 0.216, p = 0.008) and digital readiness (ß = 0.584, p < 0.001) were positively associated with the learning experience (R2 = 0.529). Readiness did not significantly moderate the affordance–experience relationship (ß = −0.015, p = 0.728). Qualitative responses highlighted immersion, flexibility and visualisation, alongside connectivity, device constraints and preferences for classroom interaction. Research limitations/implications Cross-sectional, self-reported data from one regional context limit causal inference and generalisability of the findings. Practical implications Vocational institutions should improve connectivity, device access and digital competence alongside HyFlex-VR implementation. Originality/value The findings distinguish the direct association of digital readiness with learning experience from its unsupported moderating role, suggesting an enabling capability rather than a boundary condition for digital readiness.

title: Managing a commercial bank's cash operations based on budgeting principles
abstractText: Subject. This article deals with theoretical and methodological issues of managing the cash operations of a commercial bank based on budgeting principles, as well as the economic relationships that arise in the process of planning, accounting, and controlling the costs of a bank's cash department. Objectives. The article aims to develop methodological approaches to creating a budgeting system for the cash operations of a commercial bank, including identifying cost centers, choosing calculation objects, calculating direct and overhead expenses, and justifying transfer prices and tariffs for settlement and cash services. Methods. For the study, we used analysis and synthesis, systems and process approaches, methods of financial planning, cost calculation, responsibility center accounting, as well as elements of strategic cost management. Results. The article explains why it makes sense to use a responsibility center approach in managing cash operations and points out where costs come from. The article offers an algorithm for developing an operating budget, which includes twelve consecutive steps, as well as author-developed formulas for calculating staff numbers, payroll, costs for maintaining workplaces and equipment, total costs per unit of calculation, and tariffs for cash management services. The methodological approaches to calculating collection costs and rates have been defined. Conclusions and Relevance. Cash management budgeting helps the bank coordinate its strategic, tactical, and operational goals, keep costs under control, reasonably allocate overhead, set transfer prices and rates, and also create conditions for improving the bank's competitiveness by reducing the cost of cash services. The proposed methods can be used by commercial banks when setting up an internal banking budgeting system, forming pricing policies for cash management services, evaluating the efficiency of cash departments, and optimizing cash handling costs.

title: Vibe marketing: what is it, how it works and what needs to be known?
abstractText: Purpose Vibe marketing has emerged as a culturally significant marketing phenomenon through the deliberate creation of affective cues that are compelling enough to inhabit, share and return to. This paper introduces and conceptualises vibe marketing, maps its process through a five-stage vibe lifecycle, identifies structural tensions and develops a future research agenda. Design/methodology/approach Drawing upon affect theory and consumer culture theory, the authors explore relevant literature and industry observations on vibe marketing practices across online and offline settings. The authors identify the constituent elements that distinguish vibe marketing from adjacent constructs and develop a lifecycle framework with managerial recommendations for each stage. Findings Vibe marketing is conceptualised as the deliberate orchestration of sensory, aesthetic and atmospheric stimuli by firms to trigger affective responses that consumers associate with a coherent, desirable social identity, such that those responses motivate engagement, sharing and loyalty. A five-stage vibe lifecycle (vibe sensing, vibe creating, vibe featuring, vibe popularising and vibe updating) describes how vibe marketing unfolds in practice. Three structural tensions arising from the lifecycle identify the field’s principal theoretical frontiers. Research limitations/implications This paper establishes vibe marketing as a theoretically grounded domain for scholars of interactive marketing and brand management, while providing practitioners with a process framework for managing affective brand strategy. Originality/value This is among the first scholarly papers to conceptualise vibe marketing as a distinct phenomenon in interactive marketing, grounding it in affect theory and consumer culture theory and proposing a lifecycle framework that maps how brands create, sustain and renew the affective atmospheres that drive consumer engagement.

abstractText: Subject. Value orientations, motivational patterns, and behavioral strategies of the modern consumer. Transformation of consumer behavior under the influence of the development of the platform economy. Objectives. Developing an integrated model of consumer behavior that combines current behavioral trends with existing typologies of consumer profiles. Methods. General scientific research methods were applied. The model allows tracking consumer behavior shifts and can be applied to various industry contexts. Conclusions. The research results can be taken into account when developing marketing and communication strategies, segmenting the target audience, and positioning brands.

title: University knowledge potential: Conceptualization of the concept
abstractText: Subject. This article focuses on the conceptualization and substantiation of the "university knowledge potential" concept. Objectives. The study aims to identify the relationship between knowledge and knowledge potential, systematize approaches to the essence of the knowledge potential of an organization, and analyze the differences in the knowledge potential of the university and the company. Methods. For the study, we used the methods of bibliometric content analysis, generalization, comparison, analysis and synthesis. Results. The article identifies five clusters of the "knowledge" category occurrence and other terms. It also determines the essence of the university's knowledge potential. Conclusions. In modern science, the concept of "knowledge" is interpreted extremely broadly, which does not allow building effective management systems in the knowledge economy. The research of the university's knowledge potential is the basis for the effective management model formation in the knowledge economy.

title: Cybersecurity of the digital ruble as a new field of knowledge: Subject, categories and methodology
abstractText: Subject. This article discusses the emerging system of knowledge about the digital ruble protection as a State monetary form, payment infrastructure and the institution of public trust. Objectives. The study aims to substantiate the definition of the digital ruble cybersecurity as an independent interdisciplinary field of knowledge, and define its object, subject, boundaries, axiomatic provisions, categorical apparatus and methodological basis. Methods. For the study, I used the methods of systems, structural-functional, institutional and risk-based approaches, conceptualization, comparative analysis, and targeted content analysis. Results. The article proposes the author's definition of the cybersecurity of the digital ruble, and formulates its axiomatic provisions. It also establishes that Russian and international studies are not combined into an independent subject, and introduces an interconnected system of categories. Conclusions. The independence of the new field is confirmed by a specific object, an integrative research question, its own categories and methodology. The results provide the basis for standards, cyber resilience indicators, scenario testing, applied research, and specialist training.

title: Statistical assessment of the relationship between macroeconomic factors and nickel production in Russia
abstractText: Subject. Factors determining the dynamics of nickel production in Russia. Objectives. To identify the factors influencing the volume of nickel production in Russia, as well as to assess the nature of the interrelationships between nickel production, world nickel prices, the exchange rate of the US dollar against the ruble and investments in fixed assets. Methods. The information base of the study was the annual data for 2006–2024. Methods of descriptive statistics, correlation and regression analysis, logarithmic modeling, time series stationarity tests, information criteria for choosing the lag length, Granger causality tests, cointegration analysis, ARDL approach and error correction model are used. Additionally, the sensitivity of the results to the structural periods of 2008–2009, 2020 and 2022–2024 and the exclusion of observations for 2021 was checked. Results. A moderate negative relationship has been revealed between the volume of nickel production and the exchange rate of the US dollar against the ruble. Linear and logarithmic regression models showed a statistically significant negative correlation of nickel production only with the exchange rate, whereas no statistically significant coefficients were obtained for world nickel prices and fixed asset investments. Granger's causality tests did not reveal stable short-term predictive relationships. The Johansen test and the ARDL bounds test did not provide convincing evidence of a long-term cointegration relationship. A negative and statistically significant error correction factor in the reduced ECM showed the presence of a dynamic correction mechanism. The main result for the exchange rate remains after excluding the observation for 2021. Conclusions. The development of the Russian nickel industry is explained not only by the macroeconomic factors considered, but also depends on a wider range of long-term industry and institutional conditions.

title: The development of data processing infrastructure and its impact on accounting practices in a historical context
abstractText: Subject. This article looks at the historical stages of the development of record-keeping media and computing devices, and also explains how this development has affected record-keeping in terms of new opportunities and the need for accounting to adapt to automation requirements. Objectives. The article aims to organize knowledge about the development of accounting information carriers and computing tools and study how this development has affected accounting practices from ancient times to the present day. Methods. For the study, we used a dialectical approach, observation, the synthesis of scattered information, analysis of the results obtained, as well as elements of accounting methods. Results. The article outlines the factors influencing information carriers and counting devices on the possibility of applying accounting principles and techniques, and notes the historical unevenness in the development and impact of computing tools on accounting forms and methods. The article also proposes a periodization of accounting based on its scientific and technical development, with a focus on the period using computing tools. The stage of accounting using computing tools is proposed to be broken down into seven periods of scientific and technological development of information and computing tools. Conclusions. The technology and specifics of information carriers determine the possibilities for putting certain accounting principles and methods into practice at any given historical stage. For a long time, computing devices only sped up calculations and did not directly affect accounting, until in the 20th century their development started to outpace the needs of bookkeeping. The article concludes that accounting needs to be adapted to automation requirements to get rid of existing methodological limitations.

title: Criteria for balancing the company's technology development strategy
abstractText: Subject. A balanced strategy of technological development in conditions of limited resources. Objectives. Defining criteria and parameters for evaluating a balanced strategy for technological development of companies. Methods. The research is based on the application of nonparametric regression modeling and multidimensional data analysis. Results. The calculation of the predicted average effects of the basic ratio of the efficiency of the use of production assets revealed a parabolic dependence of the criterion with the boundaries of changes in qualitative estimates in the range of 3.25–7 units. The operational component prevails within this gap, while the investment component prevails outside it. The boundaries of the segment correspond to a qualitative change in the criterion values. Conclusions. The results of the study indicate the relevance of monitoring the information consistency of classical financial and economic indicators in the dynamic market environment of the modern economy and can be used as the basis for more analytical studies of various aspects of the qualitative assessment of the balance of technological development of companies, taking into account industry specifics.

title: Assessment of Neurological Deficits Using the Stroke Impact Scale
abstractText: Background and Purpose: This study evaluated physical and social functioning using the Stroke Impact Scale (SIS) and Short Form-36 (SF-36) to assess health-related quality of life in patients following stroke.Methods: The SIS and SF-36 were administered to 278 stroke patients approximately 90 days after stroke. The SIS-16 and SF-36 Physical Functioning (PF) domain were used to assess physical functioning, while the SIS Participation and SF-36 Social Functioning (SF) domains were used to assess social functioning. Descriptive statistics and analysis of variance (ANOVA) were used to characterize physical and social functioning after stroke across different levels of the modified Rankin Scale (mRS).Results: Both the SIS-16 and SF-36 PF domains demonstrated substantial floor effects. In contrast to the SIS Participation domain, the SF-36 SF domain showed substantial ceiling effects. Both the SIS-16 and SF-36 PF domains effectively distinguished between mRS levels 0–1, 2, 3, and 4. The SIS Participation domain also distinguished between mRS levels 0–1, 2, and 3–4. However, the SF-36 SF scores were similar across mRS levels 0, 1, and 2, as well as levels 2, 3, and 4.Conclusions: Compared with the SF-36 PF and SF domains, the SIS-16 and SIS Participation domains are better able to capture physical functioning and social well-being in patients following stroke.

Patterns of "forced digital mutations" and adaptation strategies of industrial enterprises in the context of post-import development
abstractText: Subject. Identification and classification of patterns of "forced digital mutations" of industrial enterprises in the context of post-import development. Objectives. Development of algorithms for the transition from crisis adaptation to controlled evolution within the framework of the course on technological sovereignty. Methods. The research is based on a macro-level statistical pattern analysis integrating methods of system analysis, strategic management and digital economy. The empirical base is based on open aggregated data from government statistics and industry monitoring of digital maturity. Methods of longitudinal analysis, normalization of indicators and clustering were used for data processing. Results. Four basic adaptation patterns are classified: "conservation and survival", "hybrid assembly", "forced import substitution" and "innovative reverse". It has been established that only strategies involving a deep restructuring of operational and value levels create the prerequisites for a controlled evolution. A strong correlation has been revealed between the mutation trajectory and the personnel factor: the shortage of engineering and IT competencies is the main limiting condition that determines the pronounced sectoral and regional differentiation of industrial enterprises. Conclusions. The use of the concept of "forced digital mutations" makes it possible to bridge the gap between reactive survival and strategic technological sovereignty. The developed approach demonstrates that universal support measures are ineffective, and dictates the need to introduce differentiated algorithms for managing digital transformation. This ensures the transition of enterprises from tactical elimination of infrastructure gaps to proactive design of sovereign digital ecosystems.

abstractText: Sektor kelapa sawit merupakan komoditas strategis Indonesia yang rantai pasoknya melibatkan banyak aktor dengan pola saluran distribusi yang beragam, sehingga menimbulkan perbedaan efektivitas antarpola saluran. Kajian ini bertujuan membandingkan efektivitas berbagai pola rantai pasok kelapa sawit dilihat dari besaran margin pemasaran, persentase farmer's share, tingkat efisiensi rantai pasok, kadar Asam Lemak Bebas (ALB) Tandan Buah Segar (TBS), serta kelancaran waktu transportasi hulu. Penelitian dilakukan melalui studi kepustakaan (desk study) dengan menelusuri artikel jurnal ilmiah nasional dan internasional terbitan sepuluh tahun terakhir yang relevan dengan topik rantai pasok TBS kelapa sawit. Data yang dikumpulkan meliputi besaran margin pemasaran, persentase farmer's share, nilai efisiensi pemasaran, kadar ALB, dan waktu tempuh transportasi, yang selanjutnya dibandingkan menggunakan metode komparasi deskriptif antarliteratur. Sintesis awal literatur menunjukkan bahwa saluran distribusi yang lebih pendek cenderung memberikan farmer's share yang lebih tinggi dan efisiensi pemasaran yang lebih baik, sedangkan saluran yang lebih panjang berpotensi memperlama waktu tunggu TBS sehingga meningkatkan risiko kenaikan kadar ALB. Kajian ini diharapkan menjadi rujukan dalam merumuskan strategi penataan saluran distribusi kelapa sawit yang lebih efisien dan adil bagi petani.

title: Modeling of production and technological chains in single-industry towns based on the methodology of intersectoral balance
abstractText: Subject. Production and technological supply chains as a set of enterprises (links) united by the flows of products and resources, where the focus firm is the last one. In single-industry cities, a city-forming enterprise linking related manufacturers into a system can be considered as a focus company. Objectives. Substantiation of the possibility of applying the methodology of intersectoral balance as the most adequate tool for quantifying production and technological supply chains. Methods. The methodological basis consists of methods of abstraction, generalization, and matrix modeling based on the methodology of intersectoral balance. Results. It is proved that the methodology of the intersectoral balance is the most adequate tool for describing vertically integrated supply chains, which makes it possible to assess the effectiveness of their activities in terms of resources expended and achieving a given output. Conclusions. The methodology of intersectoral balance makes it possible to analyze the system of internal production links of the chain, where the focus company is the city-forming one, in order to develop practical recommendations in the field of industrial and regional policy. The considered tools can be used by firms in the supply chain, allowing them to determine the optimal options for the transition from a raw material model to a closed-cycle bioeconomy on a strict mathematical basis using digital technologies, and to design new systems with horizontal and vertical connections between firms.
