title: A system of key indicators for assessing the smoothing effect of State instruments of regional alignment
abstractText: Subject. Quantitative assessment of the smoothing effect of State instruments of regional alignment. This effect is understood as the ability of a separate tool to reduce inter-regional imbalances in the economic, social, digital and infrastructural spheres. Objectives. The construction of a methodically coherent system of key performance indicators that measures the static, structural and dynamic components of smoothing separately and allows their convolution into a single integral index. Methods. The author uses the σ- and β-convergence apparatus, the principles of constructing composite JRC/OECD indicators, as well as variational, threshold, and dynamic analysis of the distribution of regions. The empirical base was made up of Rosstat data for 2015–2024. Results. The three–level (variational – threshold – dynamic) structure of private indicators in four content blocks is substantiated. A formula for a composite smoothing index based on relative changes in normalized indicators is proposed. Testing on regional policy instruments in 2015–2024 showed weak dynamics: the coefficient of variation of the gross regional product per capita decreased from 110.4% to 105%, and the Gini coefficient returned to the pre-sanctions level of 0.408, indicating limited returns mainly from fiscal transfer mechanisms. Conclusions. The current statistical infrastructure does not separate the absolute and distributional effects of the equalization policy. The proposed system eliminates this gap by ensuring comparability of instruments and an integrated assessment of their combined impact.

title: Beyond policy rhetoric: Disability exclusion in South African higher education
abstractText: This study explored the challenges disabled students face in accessing learning facilities at the University of Limpopo, South Africa. Situated within the context of progressive national policies such as the Education White Paper 6: Special Needs Education, which are inconsistently implemented, this article addresses a critical gap between legislative rhetoric and the lived realities of students with disabilities in resource-constrained universities. The primary aim of this study was to critically investigate the systemic barriers to access to learning and their consequent impact on the academic and social inclusion of disabled students. Through qualitative interviews with ten students, persistent barriers, including inaccessible infrastructure, delayed learning materials and social exclusion, were identified. Findings reveal a significant gap between inclusive education policies and actual implementation, highlighting institutional neglect. Urgent reforms, including improved infrastructure, staff training and accountability measures, are recommended to create an equitable learning environment.

title: X-ray polarimetry of a magnetar in the aftermath of an anti-glitch. Revisiting 1E 2259+586 with IXPE
abstractText: Magnetars have been known to display timing anomalies such as glitches and anti-glitches. In particular, the anomalous X-ray pulsar whose properties in the X-ray band were recently investigated through a joint observation campaign, has been observed to have multiple glitches and three anti-glitches, the most recent occurring in May 2025. Although the X-ray emission is currently decaying, the flux, which roughly doubled at the onset of the anti-glitch, had not yet returned to its original level at the time of the observation, and the pulse profile has also shown significant evolution. We present an analysis of the recent observation of that spans ∼ 11 days, from late April to early May 2026, after its anti-glitch event in 2025. We compare the post-anti-glitch polarisation results with those obtained from the previous observation in 2023. This provides an unprecedented opportunity to monitor the spectro-polarimetric evolution of a magnetar in the wake of a hallmark event such as an anti-glitch. A dedicated 400, and Director’s Discretionary Time (DDT) observation was approved to track possible changes in the degree and angle of polarisation with respect to the pre-anti-glitch campaign. Spectral and polarimetric properties were jointly modelled within the xspec ixpeobssim suites, and the analysis was further expanded using a maximum-likelihood technique. No significant detection was found in the phase-averaged and energy-integrated spectrum of this observation. However, despite the significantly shorter exposure, polarisation was clearly detected in the phase-resolved spectrum and the degree of polarisation was found to have a higher best-fitting value, though still statistically consistent, than the previous measurement from 2023, reaching a level gtrsim30% in correspondence to the pulse profile minimum. In spite of some slight differences between the two observations, the polarisation trends remain largely consistent and indicate that the source has mostly returned to its pre-event state.

title: Improving methods for evaluating the effectiveness of investment projects in the gaming industry
abstractText: Subject. Methods for evaluating the efficiency of investment projects implemented in the gaming industry, oriented toward decision-making under conditions of high uncertainty, nonlinear cash flows, and dependence on user behavior. Objectives. To develop an adaptive system for evaluating the efficiency of investment projects in the gaming industry. Methods. Systems and scenario approaches, methods of investment analysis, and comparative analysis are used. Results. An adaptive system for evaluating the efficiency of investment projects implemented in the gaming industry is developed, including scenario modeling, a modified payback period indicator, and adapted indicators: net present value (NPV), internal rate of return, and profitability index. It is shown that taking into account the concentration of revenues in the post-release period and the factors of user activity makes it possible to improve the accuracy of the assessment and identify the key drivers of successful project implementation. A mechanism for interpreting the evaluation results is proposed based on the application of a system of project development scenarios, which makes it possible to take into account the level of investment risk. Conclusions and Relevance. The proposed approach to adapting the calculations and interpretation of the values of key indicators for evaluating the efficiency of game investment projects will make it possible to obtain a more accurate and realistic picture of their investment attractiveness and to increase the validity of investment decisions made with due regard for the industry specifics. The results can be used by game studios, investors, and publishers when making decisions on launching and financing game investment projects, as well as when developing financial models of projects and assessing their risks.

title: Unveiling the layered ecology of family math co-design with mothers, teachers and researchers
abstractText: Purpose This paper aims to examine a family math leadership team (FMLT) within a larger Research-Practice Partnership with a school serving more than 80% of Latine students. The authors center co-design as a means to materialize the equitable aims of their collaboration for family math among nondominant mothers, teachers and researchers and explore: What are the practices that emerge when mothers, teachers and researchers co-design family math activities for their school? How do these practices enable the enactment of an equitable collaboration? Design/methodology/approach Taking a qualitative approach, the authors analyzed the six meetings held during one school academic year. They followed thematic analysis to identify the patterns in the practices enacted in the conversations among mothers, teachers and researchers, engaging the mothers and teachers in the initial stage of the analyses. Findings The practices identified in the FMLT conversations unveil an ecology of family math co-design in elementary schools sustained through three interconnected layers. The individual layer highlights the practices that supported team members in creating a humanizing space and moving beyond institutionalized roles. The relational layer portrays the linguistic and socio-emotional practices enacted to create relationships rooted in authentic cariño and confianza. Finally, a systemic layer explains how the FMLT became a space for organizing and taking actions that would mobilize the school. Originality/value This study contributes a model of a layered ecology of family math co-design as a component of a larger system for instructional improvement in elementary mathematics. The authors extend the mathematical family partnership scholarship by centering a design-based approach.

title: 10 kV配电系统继电保护整定计算与运行维护
abstractText: 10 kV配电系统是用户侧供电的主要环节，继电保护配置与整定是否合理，决定了故障切除的选择性和快速性。本文结合某工业园区10 kV配电系统，论述了保护配置原则、短路电流计算、过流与速断保护整定、变压器保护配置以及运行维护要点，分析了整定计算中上下级配合、灵敏系数校验和电动机自启动影响等关键问题。实践表明，按阶梯原则整定并逐级校验灵敏系数后，保护动作选择性明显改善，馈线故障切除时间由0.5 s缩短至0.2 s，因越级跳闸造成的全站停电由每年4次降为0次，保护正确动作率达到99.2%。

abstractText: This study examines the interrelationship between hydraulic and physicochemical processes in the integrated processing of Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris L.) needles. The research addresses the need to coordinate operating conditions for aqueous extract production and subsequent utilization of the fibrous residue. The aim is to provide a theoretical basis for determining the water volume, extraction time, and material purification conditions. The methodology employs mass and energy balances, phase equilibrium and mass transfer kinetics equations, and differential analysis. Analytical expressions are derived for the extract concentration and the amount of extractives remaining in the material during an isothermal batch process. The effects of liquid retention on the actual product yield and the carryover of soluble substances to the subsequent stage are established. The minimum extraction time and the condition for achieving a specified yield are determined. Under the equilibrium approximation and assuming a linear relationship between specific energy consumption and water volume, an expression for the energy-efficient water volume is obtained. Dimensionless calculations indicate that the yield at maximum energy efficiency is 0.5635, compared with the target value of 0.60. The residue mass balance is coupled with a kinetic model of alkaline treatment. An allowable treatment time interval is established subject to constraints on the proportion and retention of the target fibrous fraction. The allocation of water among successive washing stages under complete mixing is justified. The influence of mechanical dewatering on subsequent drying is determined. The derived relationships are verified through dimensional analysis, limiting-case analysis, and numerical integration. Practical application of the proposed model requires experimental determination of its coefficients for the specific feedstock composition.

title: Not less documented, but differently attributed: descriptive warrant and named-maker metadata in two museum dress collections
abstractText: Purpose A catalog record can describe an object in detail yet name no maker. A missing maker name can mean a thinner record, a name never collected (collecting history) or a descriptive tradition recording place and technique (descriptive warrant). The paper tests the thinner-record explanation and proposes element-by-element auditing. Design/methodology/approach The analysis covered 47,537 dress-related records from two Western museums, the Metropolitan Museum of Art (Met) and the Victoria and Albert Museum (V&A), plus 19,764 Met records across 14 departments. A dictionary of 1,098 place and culture name patterns coded region. The Western/non-Western grouping describes museum classification, not the objects or cultures. V&A completeness was scored from five non-maker prose fields. Findings At the V&A, 48.5% of Western and 6.2% of non-Western records named a maker. Non-Western records were not systematically less populated across the measured non-maker fields. Adjusting for non-maker documentation changed the difference from 42.3 to 43.5 points. It persisted within production period and object type, holding in 9 of 9 object types produced 1850–1969, and at the Met outside its Japanese records. Descriptive warrant, collecting history and later cataloging practice remain plausible explanations. The exploratory association between department and named maker was stable at one museum only. Originality/value Earlier studies measured what collections make visible. This study measures the maker element and shows cultural asymmetry can occur there in otherwise extensively documented records.
